papers.authors: McLachlan MJ, Bettcher B, Langhough R, DiFilippo A, Betthauser T, McVea A, LeMerise L, Zammit M, Grover E, Jonaitis EM, Ennis G, Chin N, Asthana S, Johnson SC, Bendlin BB, Christian BT.
papers.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
papers.abstract: Introduction Synaptic loss is one of the strongest post-mortem predictors of Alzheimer's disease (AD) severity and may impact how pathology affects cognition. This study compared regional [11 C]UCB-J synaptic density across the AD continuum and evaluated the extent to which synaptic density mediates relationships between AD biomarkers. Methods Seventy-two participants completed PET scans, MRIs, and cognitive testing. Participants were categorized into subgroups representing typical AD progression. Regional synaptic density was compared across subgroups and pathological variables. Standard mediation and moderated mediation analyses were performed using amyloid and tau as predictors/moderators and MoCA score as outcome. Results The amyloid+/tau+/impaired subgroup showed lower synaptic density than controls, particularly for transverse temporal, inferior parietal, and hippocampal regions (Cohen's d=1.60, 1.57, 1.50). Hippocampal synaptic density had the strongest associations with tau (β=-0.473); transverse temporal synaptic density had the strongest association with amyloid (β=-0.543) and age (β=-0.614). Eight of twelve assessed brain regions demonstrated significant indirect effects across mediation frameworks. The inferior parietal lobe showed the largest mediation for amyloid (45.3%) and tau (28.9%). Discussion These findings support the hypothesis that synaptic loss is a primary mechanism contributing to clinical AD and suggest that synaptic density imaging can provide complementary information to the existing AD framework.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Cerebral blood flow-oxygen metabolism uncoupling at 24 hours after stroke thrombectomy.
papers.authors: Lomahan CA, Kalarakis G, Luby M, Holmin S, Lundberg J, Mazya MV, Latour LL, Arnberg-Sandor F.
papers.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
papers.abstract: BackgroundFollowing successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke, tissue with abnormal perfusion may have impaired oxygen extraction and metabolism. MRI model-based oxygen extraction fraction (OEFmax) and cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO2) were characterized in hypoperfusion and hyperemia regions 24 hours post-EVT.MethodsEighty-four patients were included with anterior circulation vessel occlusion, successful recanalization, and an MRI at 24 hours post-EVT. Time-to-maximum (Tmax) and cerebral blood flow (CBF) were evaluated for hypoperfusion and hyperemia. CBF, OEFmax, and CMRO2 were quantified using i) segmentation-based and ii) single slice region of interest (ROI) analyses. Normalized CBF, OEFmax, and CMRO2 were calculated by dividing the segmentation or ROI value by the contralateral value.ResultsSixty-seven (80%) patients had abnormal perfusion; hypoperfusion in 22 (26%), hyperemia in 36 (43%), and both in 9 (11%). Compared to control, hypoperfused regions demonstrated a 62% CBF decrease, 52% CMRO2 decrease, and 68% OEFmax increase (p<0.01). Hyperemic regions demonstrated a 58% CBF increase, 26% CMRO2 increase, and 25% OEFmax decrease (p<0.01). Hyperemia had no significant correlation between normalized CBF and CMRO2 (p=0.14).ConclusionHyperemia regions demonstrated cerebral blood flow-oxygen metabolism uncoupling, suggesting the underlying mechanism as loss of cerebrovascular autoregulation rather than hypermetabolic demand.

papers.title: The Pallidothalamic Tract in Functional Neurosurgery: A Systematic Review.
papers.authors: Al-Smadi MW, Al-Khafaji YQ, Aslan S, Giampiccolo D, Xu SS, Akram H, Limousin P, Foltynie T, Zrinzo L, Krueger MT.
papers.abstract: Background The pallidothalamic tract (PTT), formed by convergence of the ansa lenticularis and fasciculus lenticularis at Forel's field H1, is a major basal ganglia efferent pathway and an emerging functional neurosurgical target. No systematic review has previously synthesised outcomes across PTT-targeted interventions. Methods This PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251248260). PubMed, OVID, and Web of Science were searched for studies reporting functional neurosurgical outcomes targeting the PTT or Forel's fields. Prospective and retrospective studies, case series, and case reports were eligible. Methodological quality was assessed using design-appropriate risk-of-bias tools. Results Forty studies encompassing 483 patients (1966-2025) were included across five modalities: MR-guided focused ultrasound (n=143), radiofrequency ablation (n=167), deep brain stimulation (n=40), cryogenic lesioning (n=82), and oil-wax injection (n=52). Mean follow-up was 21 months. In Parkinson disease (11 studies; n=135), mean UPDRS-III improvement was 39%, with reductions in dyskinesia (UDysRS 90%) and tremor (75%). In dystonia (12 studies; n=87), BFMDRS and TWSTRS improved by 57% and 47%, respectively. Dual-target strategies, particularly PTT-VIM combinations, showed additive effects, including greater tremor reduction (77%) and improved rigidity. In drug-resistant epilepsy (6 studies; n=157), seizure reduction occurred in 71% and seizure freedom in 33%. Conclusions PTT-targeted interventions yield meaningful motor improvements in Parkinson disease and dystonia, with preliminary evidence supporting additive dual-target benefits. Seizure-reducing effects in refractory epilepsy have been reported. Evidence remains limited by small uncontrolled studies, heterogeneous outcomes, and inconsistent adverse-event reporting. Prospective trials will elucidate the efficacy, safety, and clinical role of the PTT in neurosurgery.

papers.title: Saponin extract from Astragalus membranaceus (Fisch.) Bunge regulates gut-brain axis through intestinal Escherichia coli to reduce cerebral oxidative stress to treat vascular dementia in rodents.
papers.authors: Yin W, He C, Gu S, Li L, Bian Y, Lu W, Xie M, Li Z, Yang Z, Wang Q.
papers.abstract: Background and purpose Vascular dementia (VD) is a cognitive dysfunction syndrome caused by cerebrovascular diseases. Astragalus membranaceus (Fisch.) Bunge (AS) has antioxidative, gut microbiota-regulating, and cognitive-improving effects. Escherichia coli (E. coli) abundance is associated with cognitive dysfunction. This study explored the mechanism by which AS improves VD by regulating E. coli along the gut-brain axis, providing a basis for VD drug research and development. Experimental approach VD models were established by permanent ligation of the common carotid artery. Morris water maze, Doppler cerebral blood flow measurement, blood lipid assays, pathological staining, Western blot, and ELISA were used to evaluate AS's protective effects on the brain. 16S rRNA sequencing analyzed gut microbiota to screen differential strains. Metabolomics screened endogenous differential metabolites. Oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) was established to evaluate 5-aminovaleric acid effects on neuronal mitochondrial function and oxidative stress. Key results AS significantly improved cognitive dysfunction, restored cerebral blood flow, and attenuated abnormal protein accumulation and oxidative stress in VD rat brains. Microbiota analysis revealed that AS inhibited E. coli proliferation and mitigated associated pathological damage. Furthermore, endogenous metabolite 5-aminovaleric acid alleviated OGD-induced neuronal damage and oxidative stress. Conclusion and implications AS can treat cognitive dysfunction and brain injury in rodents, regulate gut microbiota balance, and reduce the contribution of E. coli. Meanwhile, AS-regulated endogenous metabolite 5-aminovaleric acid can also treat OGD-induced nerve cell injury. These findings suggest that AS may be a promising candidate for VD treatment and provide mechanistic insight into gut-brain axis regulation.

papers.title: Management of seizures in patients with brain tumors.
papers.authors: Koh HY, Tobochnik S.
papers.abstract: Purpose of review Discoveries relating to the cancer neuroscience of gliomas have reframed brain tumor-related epilepsy (BTRE) as the product of reciprocal interactions at the neural-tumor interface. This framework provides the rationale for targeted strategies to optimize both seizure control and brain tumor survival outcomes. Recent findings Feedforward dynamics involving hyperexcitability and cellular proliferation in glioma-infiltrated cortex drive synaptic remodeling of neural circuits that correlate with shorter survival. Seizure assessment metrics demonstrate that worsening seizure control may precede or align with progressive disease. In this context, early evidence indicates a potential role for targeted tumor-directed therapy in addition to antiseizure medications (ASMs) for optimizing seizure control. Noncontrolled studies evaluating ASM tapering strategies in BTRE suggest that tumor stability is more important for seizure control than the duration of seizure freedom. Summary BTRE involves dynamic and fluctuating seizure risk driven by tumor biology, tumor-directed therapy, and treatment response. Hyperexcitability at the cellular level and clinical seizure activity are increasingly understood as a reflection of tumor biology and a potentially modifiable target to improve outcomes. The addition of seizure assessments as secondary endpoints in brain tumor clinical trials may lead to a refined individualized and disease-specific approach to ASM management.

papers.title: The network localization and underlying biological basis of heterogeneous structural and functional brain abnormalities in insomnia disorder.
papers.authors: Xue W, Gao Z, Shi Y, Zhang Y, Du W, Tao B, Zhu F, Wan Q, Zhang W, Lui S, Lu P, Tang X, Xiao Y.
papers.abstract: Insomnia disorder (ID) has become a prevalent sleep disorder worldwide, yet its underlying neural mechanisms remain unclear due to heterogeneous neuroimaging findings and uncertain network localization. We identified brain structural and functional abnormality locations associated with ID from 63 published neuroimaging studies, including 3391 patients and 3433 healthy controls. Using coordinate network mapping combined with a normative connectome database, we mapped these abnormalities to large-scale brain networks of ID across imaging modalities and further decoded them by integrating microscale chemo-architectural, cellular, and cognitive maps. The structural network widely involved the ventral attention (VAN), sensorimotor (SMN), dorsal attention (DAN) and default mode network (DMN); the task-induced network showed a similar but less extensive pattern, predominantly implicating the VAN, DMN, SMN and subcortical network (SCN); in contrast, the resting-state network was largely confined to the left middle frontal gyrus and the bilateral mid-cingulate cortex. Molecular mapping revealed both shared and distinct neurotransmitter signatures across the three networks, involving cholinergic, histaminergic, glutamatergic, noradrenergic, and opioid systems. Cellular decoding showed relatively selective associations of the structural and task-based networks with glial cells and excitatory neurons, whereas the resting-state network exhibited broader associations with glial cells and multiple excitatory and inhibitory neuronal subtypes. Cognitive decoding linked structural and task-based networks to sensorimotor processing and the resting-state network to memory-related functions. Our findings reconcile heterogeneous neuroimaging results and reveal neurobiological substrates of ID from a network perspective, providing a promising biomarker and paving the way for circuit-based precision therapies of ID.

papers.title: ADHDeepNet: An Explainable Framework for EEG-Based ADHD Detection From Raw Signals.
papers.authors: Amini A, Alijanpour Shalmani M, Latifi B, Nasrabadi AM.
papers.abstract: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a common brain disorder in children that can persist into adulthood, affecting social, academic, and career life. Early diagnosis is crucial for managing these impacts on patients and the healthcare system but is often labor-intensive and time-consuming. This paper presents a novel method to improve ADHD diagnosis precision and timeliness by leveraging Deep Learning (DL) approaches and electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. We introduce ADHDeepNet, a deep learning model that utilizes comprehensive temporal-spatial characterization, attention modules, and explainability techniques optimized for EEG signals. ADHDeepNet integrates feature extraction and refinement processes to enhance ADHD diagnosis. The model was trained and validated on a dataset of 121 participants (61 ADHD, 60 Healthy Controls), employing nested cross-validation for robust performance. The proposed two-stage methodology uses a 10-fold cross-subject validation strategy. Initially, each iteration optimizes the model's hyper-parameters with inner 2-fold cross-validation. Then, Additive Gaussian Noise (AGN) with various standard deviations and magnification levels is applied for data augmentation. ADHDeepNet achieved 100% sensitivity and 99.17% accuracy in classifying ADHD/HC subjects. To clarify model explainability and identify key brain regions and frequency bands for ADHD diagnosis, we analyzed the learned weights and activation patterns of the model's primary layers. Additionally, t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) visualized high-dimensional data, aiding in interpreting the model's decisions. This study highlights the potential of deep learning and EEG in enhancing ADHD diagnosis accuracy and efficiency.

papers.title: Intranasal administration of enalapril confers acute neuroprotection by mitigating mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis in a rat model of ischemic stroke.
papers.authors: Sadeghian N, Salimpour Azar S, Shadman J, Abedi A, Salimi A, Alipour MR, Panahpour H.
papers.abstract: Background Stroke remains a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide, with effective treatments hindered by its complex pathophysiology. This study is the first to explore the neuroprotective potential of intranasal enalapril, in mitigating ischemic stroke outcomes through its influence on mitochondrial function. Methods Male Sprague-Dawley rats were subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO), followed by the intranasal administration of enalapril (0.03 mg/kg) post-ischemia. Neurological function was evaluated after 24 hours of reperfusion through the modified neurological severity score (mNSS), grip strength, and hot plate tests. Brain infarct volume was quantified via Triphenyltetrazolium chloride staining. Blood- brain barrier (BBB) integrity was evaluated via the Evans Blue extravasation assay. Additionally, we employed immunofluorescence techniques to assess apoptosis through TUNEL staining and evaluated mitochondrial function by examining mitochondrial swelling, succinate dehydrogenase activity, mitochondrial membrane potential and reactive oxygen species production. Results Intranasal administration of enalapril significantly reduced the infarct volume, preserved BBB integrity, and attenuated sensorimotor deficits in MCAO rats. These protective effects were closely associated with enhanced regional cerebral blood flow, a significant reduction in neuronal apoptosis, and improved mitochondrial function. Conclusion Intranasal enalapril may provide a novel approach to neuroprotection in ischemic stroke, potentially through mechanisms that enhance mitochondrial function and reduce neuronal apoptosis.

papers.title: Jujuboside A inhibits the progression of ischaemic stroke by regulating miR-583.
papers.authors: Yuan T, Guo Z.
papers.journal: Xenobiotica; the fate of foreign compounds in biological systems
papers.abstract: 1. objective Jujuboside A (JuA) possesses anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities; however, its role and mechanisms of action in ischaemic stroke (IS) remain unclear. 2. methods A mice MCAO was established to evaluate the effects of different doses of JuA on brain water content, neurological function scores, behavioural parameters, inflammatory factors, and oxidative stress markers. An OGD model was established in SH-SY5Y cells. Cell viability and apoptosis were assessed by the CCK-8 assay and flow cytometry. Inflammatory factors were evaluated via ELISA, and oxidative stress markers were assessed by commercial kits. RT-qPCR was used to analyse changes in miR-583 expression under OGD conditions. 3. results JuA dose-dependently alleviated cerebral edoema, neurological deficits, and motor dysfunction in MCAO mice; it reduced TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, MDA, and LDH, and increased SOD levels. Under OGD conditions, JuA (40 μM) significantly improved SH-SY5Y cell viability and reduced cell apoptosis, inflammatory responses, and oxidative stress. Furthermore, inhibition of miR-583 abolished the protective effects of JuA. 4. conclusion By upregulating miR-583 to suppress inflammation and oxidative stress, JuA alleviates IS injury and represents a promising candidate neuroprotective compound.

papers.title: Schaftoside, a functional flavonoid from fenugreek (Trigonella foenum-graecum L.), alleviates depression and cognitive deficits via the microbiome-gut-brain axis in stressed mice.
papers.authors: Dai Y, Song P, Cheng C, Cheng L, Dai C, Lu W.
papers.abstract: Depression involves dysregulation of central and peripheral networks, with gut microbiota alterations increasingly implicated in pathogenesis. Trigonella foenum-graecum L. (fenugreek), a functional food and medicinal herb, has been used traditionally for neurological disorders, yet its specific neuroprotective constituents remain poorly characterized. This study evaluated the antidepressant potential of schaftoside, the predominant flavonoid of fenugreek seed flavonoids, and explored its mechanisms involving the microbiome-gut-brain axis in a chronic restraint stress (CRS) mouse model. Male Kunming mice were subjected to CRS and orally administered schaftoside (20, 50, and 125 mg kg-1 ) or fluoxetine (10 mg kg-1 ) for 28 days. Behavioral assessments (tail suspension, forced swim, novel object recognition, and Y-maze) demonstrated that schaftoside dose-dependently ameliorated depressive-like behaviors and cognitive impairments. It attenuated hippocampal neuronal damage and neuroinflammation, restoring hippocampal 5-HT, NE, and ACh levels. Intestinal barrier integrity was improved, evidenced by enhanced tight junction proteins (ZO-1, occludin) and mucin (MUC2) expression, alongside reduced colonic pro-inflammatory cytokines and elevated IL-10. 16S rRNA profiling revealed that schaftoside reshaped gut microbiota composition, notably suppressing stress-enriched Bacteroides and promoting butyrate-producing Butyricicoccus . Untargeted metabolomics identified restoration of tryptophan and α-linolenic acid metabolism pathways. Spearman correlation analysis revealed significant associations between specific gut genera, fecal metabolites, and host inflammatory/neurochemical markers. Hippocampal transcriptomics indicated enrichment of cAMP signaling, dopaminergic, and serotonergic synapse pathways. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from schaftoside-treated donors partially recapitulated the behavioral, anti-inflammatory, and intestinal barrier-protective effects in antibiotic-pretreated recipient mice, accompanied by restoration of the gut microbiota and metabolite profiles. These findings demonstrate that schaftoside, the major flavonoid of fenugreek seeds, exhibits promising antidepressant-like potential through modulation of the microbiome-gut-brain axis, supporting the functional food application of fenugreek-derived flavonoids for stress-related mood disorders.

papers.title: Effect sizes for brain-based predictive models of cognition across the lifespan.
papers.authors: Christensen E, Wiersch L, Wang M, McPherson B, Shearer H, Noble S, Lam K, Poline JB, Dhamala E.
papers.abstract: Brain-based predictive models offer a promising approach to understanding individual differences in cognitive functioning across the lifespan. This review synthesizes current literature on brain-based cognitive predictions using large-scale datasets, examining how methodological choices and data-related factors impact model performance. We find that brain-based predictive models demonstrate relatively consistent, albeit wide ranging performance across the lifespan, explaining approximately 10-40% of variance in cognitive abilities. Key findings include: (1) models perform better when predicting general cognitive ability compared to specific functions; (2) crystallized abilities are more predictable than fluid abilities; (3) task-based functional connectivity generally outperforms resting-state approaches in younger populations, while structural measures become superior predictors in older adults; (4) multimodal approaches using hierarchical stacked models optimize prediction accuracy; and (5) elastic net and ridge regression provide optimal balance between predictive performance and computational efficiency. In summary, we propose methodological advances to improve the precision and utility of brain-based cognitive predictions.

papers.title: Dysregulated cholesterol trafficking through ABCA1 drives neurodegeneration in Parkinson's disease.
papers.authors: Ma FX, Zhao XX, Wang XX, Fang SY, Xu SH, Wang M, Liu YX, Wang C, Wang QL, Lu M, Cao L.
papers.abstract: Although brain cholesterol dysregulation is implicated in Parkinson's disease (PD), targeting cholesterol synthesis has shown limited efficacy. Here we identify ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1) as a critical regulator of cholesterol homeostasis in PD. We show that ABCA1 expression is elevated in the substantia nigra of postmortem PD brains and in a PD mouse model, with regional analyses revealing preferential alterations in nigral and striatal circuits. Mechanistically, astrocytic ABCA1 drives excessive cholesterol efflux in mice, promoting neuronal cholesterol overload. In neurons, ABCA1 localizes to lysosomes, where it facilitates cholesterol import, leading to cholesterol accumulation, autophagy impairment and α-synuclein pathology. Genetic silencing of Abca1 in either astrocytes or dopaminergic neurons attenuates neurodegeneration and behavioral deficits in vivo. Furthermore, we identify magnesium citrate as an ABCA1 inhibitor and show that it reduces dopaminergic neuronal loss in a PD mouse model. Our findings identify an ABCA1-dependent cholesterol pathway underlying PD pathogenesis and support ABCA1 inhibition as a potential disease-modifying strategy.

papers.title: Dual-Interface Engineering of Cs2CuBiBr6-Based Memristive Synaptic Devices for Neuromorphic Computing.
papers.authors: Kim CE, Cho S, Choi YS, Lee JY, Lee D, Kim J, Kang DW, Ha TJ.
papers.abstract: Pb-free double perovskite Cs2CuBiBr6 (CCBB)-based resistive random-access memory (ReRAM) synaptic devices are developed using a dual-interface engineering approach to achieve stable resistive switching and neuromorphic functionality. High-quality CCBB thin films are obtained via optimized antisolvent-assisted crystallization, enabling enhanced crystallinity and reduced defect-induced energetic disorder. Modification of the bottom interface with a poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) interlayer improves CCBB film continuity and provides a more favorable environment for homogeneous charge injection. The introduction of an ultrathin bathocuproine (BCP) interlayer at the top interface regulates the spatial redistribution of Ag-related species. The cooperative regulation of charge injection and Ag-related electro-ionic processes promotes more reproducible formation and rupture of localized conductive pathways, resulting in improved switching stability and device-to-device reproducibility. The CCBB-based ReRAM exhibits reliable bipolar resistive switching over 600 cycles, an on/off current ratio of approximately 103, and stable data retention up to 104 s. Gradual and repeatable conductance modulation under electrical pulse stimulation further demonstrates synaptic potentiation and depression behaviors. MNIST-based neural network simulations reveal excellent neuromorphic performance, with up to 90% recognition accuracy. This work highlights cooperative dual-interface regulation of charge injection and Ag-related electro-ionic processes as an effective design strategy for achieving reliable Pb-free perovskite ReRAM and neuromorphic synaptic operation.

papers.title: Machine learning of connectome-wide functional connectivity in spinal muscular atrophy.
papers.authors: Li Y, Cai H, Zhang M, Yan M, Lan S, Nie H, Shen W, Yan C, Xu B, Liang Y, Tang W, Li Y, Xiang P, Chen Y.
papers.abstract: While traditional view posed SMA as a pure motor neuron disorder, accumulating evidence pointed to the broader involvement of central nervous system. This study aimed to combined connectome-wide resting-state functional connectivity with machine learning algorithms to investigate the underlying brain mechanisms in SMA and capture the potential neuroimaging biomarker. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging were acquired from 43 SMA (26 SMA type 2 and 17 type 3) and 45 healthy controls (HCs). Connectome-wide functional connectivity, defined based on the Automated Anatomical Labeling 116 atlas (AAL116), combined with machine learning algorithms including logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM) and random forest (RF) were conducted for SMA vs HCs and SMA type 2 vs 3 classification. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) algorithm was used to quantify the contribution of individual connections. Connectome-wide functional connectivity allowed individual classification of SMA and HCs with stable performance across machine learning models. The majority of the most discriminative functional connectivity involved the high-level associative regions and cerebellum, subserving sensory and motor processing. Furthermore, the functional connectivity between right superior parietal gyrus and right inferior temporal gyrus was positively correlated with motor function. In conclusion, our study provided connectome-wide evidence that functional connectivity patterns involving high-level associative cortices and the cerebellum could distinguish SMA from HCs using machine learning. The identified connectivity features offer new insight into the distributed brain pathology of SMA beyond the traditional classical motor neuron view, and may serve as promising neuroimaging marker for this disease.

papers.title: Resting-state fMRI biomarkers of surgical outcome in temporal lobe epilepsy: Network reorganization, rsfMRI-based prediction models, and cognition - A systematic review.
papers.authors: Xu CMC, Marstrand-Joergensen MR, McCulloch DE, Pinborg LH.
papers.abstract: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is a network disorder extending beyond the structurally defined epileptogenic zone. Resting-state functional MRI (rsfMRI) may provide information on brain network alterations relevant to seizure outcome and cognitive risk after epilepsy surgery. We reviewed rsfMRI studies in TLE surgical cohorts to evaluate postoperative network changes, preoperative predictors of seizure outcome, and associations between functional connectivity and cognition. This systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO. Fifteen studies were included, comprising 474 TLE patients who underwent resective epilepsy surgery and had at least 1 year of follow-up. Studies were reviewed for patient population, surgery, rsfMRI methodology, networks or regions, outcome definition, postoperative network changes, and cognitive assessments. Despite heterogeneity in patient selection, surgery, rsfMRI analysis, and outcome definition, studies consistently reported reduced DMN-related connectivity in TLE compared with healthy controls. Postoperative functional connectivity in seizure-free patients shifted toward healthy controls patterns in few studies. Preoperative rsfMRI-based prediction models showed promising accuracy for predicting seizure outcome but were generally developed in small cohorts and lacked external validation. Evidence relating rsfMRI to cognition was limited, but implicated thalamic, ascending reticular activating system, and thalamo-occipital connectivity in attention, language, and executive functions. RsfMRI is a promising research biomarker for network-level risk stratification in TLE surgery, particularly for seizure outcome prediction and postoperative network reorganization. Current evidence remains insufficient for clinical implementation. Future studies require larger homogeneous multicenter cohorts, standardized acquisition and preprocessing, consistent outcome definitions, systematic postoperative rsfMRI, neuropsychological assessment, and external validation of prediction models.

papers.title: Interpersonal neural synchrony and parent-child behaviors during naturalistic interactions: A systematic review.
papers.authors: De Leener M, Sfeir M, Galdiolo S, Rossignol M.
papers.abstract: Interpersonal neural synchrony (INS), defined as the temporal alignment of neural activity between socially interacting individuals, has been proposed as an index of parent-child interaction quality. However, its relationship with moment-to-moment adjustment of parent-child behavior remains insufficiently understood. This systematic review examined associations between INS and observable behavior during naturalistic parent-child interactions, the factors influencing these associations, and the methods used to investigate them. Following PRISMA guidelines, systematic searches of Scopus, PubMed, and ScienceDirect identified 15 peer-reviewed empirical studies involving children from preschool age to early adolescence. INS-behavior associations were heterogeneous across studies. Higher INS was most consistently associated with mutual engagement, shared positive affect, and supportive parenting, whereas findings concerning reciprocity, responsiveness, and child agency were more context-dependent. Time-resolved analyses further indicated that INS fluctuated in relation to specific behavioral events and revealed temporally asymmetric patterns in which parent or child neural activity preceded that of the interaction partner. However, these patterns do not establish causal directionality and may partly reflect shared exposure to task-related or interactional inputs. Task structure and the availability of direct social cues appeared to shape INS-behavior associations, while parental stress and child social functioning emerged as potential sources of variability in INS. Methodologically, the findings highlight the value of combining micro- and macro-level behavioral coding with time-resolved and directionality-sensitive analyses, alongside stronger controls for spurious synchrony and common inputs. Given the limited number and methodological heterogeneity of available studies, the findings should be regarded as preliminary and primarily hypothesis-generating.

papers.title: White Matter Hyperintensities of Presumed Vascular Origin: Current Understanding of Development and Progression.
papers.authors: Shang T.
papers.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
papers.abstract: Background and purpose White matter hyperintensities (WMH) of presumed vascular origin are among the most common MRI manifestations of cerebral small vessel disease and are a major contributor to vascular contributions to cognitive impairment and dementia. Although WMH have traditionally been attributed to chronic ischemia resulting from small vessel pathology, the biological mechanisms underlying their development and, more importantly, their progression remain incompletely understood. Recent advances in longitudinal neuroimaging, quantitative MRI, pathology, genetics, and physiological imaging have substantially expanded our understanding of WMH progression, making this an appropriate time to evaluate current concepts and synthesize emerging evidence. Observations We review contemporary evidence regarding the biological processes implicated in WMH development and progression, including hypertension and vascular risk factors, acute ischemic injury, chronic hypoperfusion, blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction, endothelial activation and vascular inflammation, arterial stiffness, intracranial artery dolichoectasia (IADE), altered cerebral fluid dynamics and genetic susceptibility. Longitudinal studies demonstrate that WMH exhibit dynamic trajectories characterized by progression, stability, and partial regression, indicating that lesion evolution is not uniformly irreversible. Pathological and advanced neuroimaging studies show that WMH represent heterogeneous tissue injury involving demyelination, axonal loss, gliosis, interstitial fluid accumulation, and microvascular abnormalities. Hypertension and blood pressure variability are consistently associated with greater WMH burden and progression, whereas baseline WMH burden is the strongest predictor of future lesion expansion. Acute ischemic lesions detected by diffusion-weighted imaging contribute to, but account for only a minority of WMH progression. Longitudinal studies evaluating cerebral perfusion, BBB permeability, inflammation, arterial stiffness, IADE and cerebral fluid dynamics have yielded variable findings but, together with genetic evidence, support roles of BBB leakage, vascular inflammation, chronic hypoperfusion, arterial and extracellular-matrix remodeling, and impaired interstitial fluid clearance in WMH progression. Conclusions Emerging evidence supports a paradigm in which WMH are viewed as a dynamic manifestation of progressive neurovascular dysfunction rather than the consequence of chronic ischemia alone. Current data suggest that early neurovascular injury evolves into a potentially self-reinforcing process characterized by persistent BBB disruption, vascular inflammation, chronic hypoperfusion, altered fluid dynamics, and recurrent ischemic injury, collectively contributes to WMH progression. Future multimodal longitudinal studies integrating cerebral hemodynamics, neurovascular function and intracranial arterial remodeling will be essential to understand WMH progression.

papers.title: Right putaminal gray matter change tracks psychomotor recovery after accelerated iTBS in melancholic treatment-resistant depression.
papers.authors: Mao D, Wu GR, Cavendish BA, De Smet S, De Witte S, Baeken C.
papers.abstract: Background Psychomotor retardation is a prominent and disabling feature of melancholic depression. Accelerated intermittent theta-burst stimulation (aiTBS) may hasten antidepressant effects, but neural substrates of early symptom improvement remain unclear. Given the central role of frontostriatal circuitry in motivation and behavioral activation, structural alterations in the striatum may represent a possible neural substrate of early therapeutic change. Methods Structural MRI was acquired from 61 patients with melancholic TRD and 77 healthy controls, and voxel-based morphometry was used to assess baseline striatal gray matter volume differences. Patients then underwent a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial of left dorsolateral prefrontal aiTBS, comprising 20 sessions over four days. In 50 patients with complete pre- and post-treatment data, we tested whether GMV change in the baseline-identified striatal region was associated with clinical change in the active and sham groups (n = 25 each). Results Patients showed greater right putamen GMV than controls at baseline. After active aiTBS, greater right putamen GMV increase was associated with greater psychomotor retardation improvement. This association was absent after sham stimulation and was not observed for overall depression severity. Conclusion The right putamen appears structurally altered in melancholic TRD. After active aiTBS, short-term putamen GMV increase was associated with psychomotor rather than broader depressive improvement. This pattern should not be interpreted as structural normalization but may reflect a relationship between putaminal change and early psychomotor recovery.

papers.title: Somatic variants in focal cortical malformations.
papers.authors: Czajewski I, Baulac S, Baldassari S.
papers.abstract: Cortical malformations are a frequent cause of infantile drug-resistant epilepsy. Somatic variants in only a fraction of brain cells are now an established cause of cortical malformations found in epilepsy surgical resections. Recent major technological and conceptual advances have improved our understanding of such mosaic neurodevelopmental disorders. Here, we review the genetics and neuropathology of focal cortical malformations caused by somatic mosaicism, focusing on the mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway-related focal cortical dysplasia type II and the glycosylation-defective mild malformation of cortical development with oligodendroglial hyperplasia in epilepsy (MOGHE). We discuss technical implementations and remaining challenges in the detection of low-level somatic variants and highlight how single-cell approaches have provided new insights into the disease mechanisms. Further, we cover the recent in vivo efforts to better characterize MOGHE, a newly defined cortical malformation.

papers.title: Sex-divergent neurovascular and cognitive effects of chronic cerebral hypoperfusion.
papers.authors: Kirby BD, Clary BL, Burrage E, Chantler PD, Dakhlallah D, Karelina K, Brown CM, Simpkins JW.
papers.abstract: Chronic cerebral hypoperfusion is the leading risk factor for the development of vascular dementia and is associated with white matter damage and cognitive impairment. Here, we assessed sex differences in vascular and neural pathology and cognitive impairment in the asymmetric carotid arterial stenosis (ACAS) mouse model of chronic cerebral hypoperfusion. Thirty days of ACAS significantly reduced cerebral blood flow, increased microvascular permeability as evidenced by extravasation of IgG and fibrinogen into brain parenchyma, and impaired MCA vasodilation. ACAS also induced white matter damage in the hippocampus and corpus callosum, with greater damage in the corpus callosum of females compared to males. Spatial memory impairments on the Barnes maze were significantly greater in ACAS males than in females. Finally, miRNA analyses revealed upregulated angiogenic miRNA in the hippocampus and cortex in ACAS females and upregulated neuroinflammatory miRNA in the hippocampus and cortex in ACAS males. Together, these findings indicate that the ACAS model produces robust neuropathology and sex differences in spatial memory and miRNA profiles.

papers.title: Intrinsic and extrinsic connectivity of the seizure onset zone at rest and during stimulation.
papers.authors: LaRocque JJ, Ojemann WKS, Xu J, Lucas A, Sinha N, Cornblath EJ, Armstrong C, Tomlinson S, Marsh ED, Sinha SR, Litt B, Davis K, Cao Q, Conrad EC.
papers.abstract: Background About half of patients who undergo epilepsy surgery for drug-resistant epilepsy have seizure recurrence, supporting the need for approaches that more accurately identify the epileptogenic zone, defined as the brain areas whose removal causes cessation of seizures. Altered network connectivity has emerged as a candidate biomarker of the epileptogenic zone, but how connectivity is altered in the epileptogenic zone remains uncertain, with prior studies reporting inconsistent results. Hypothesis We hypothesized that a difference in intrinsic versus extrinsic connectivity of the epileptogenic zone may explain prior discrepant findings. Methods We retrospectively studied a multicenter cohort of 37 adult and 42 pediatric patients who underwent intracranial EEG recording and brain stimulation as part of epilepsy surgery planning. We measured spontaneous connectivity using Pearson correlation and perturbational connectivity using stimulation evoked potentials, modeling the connectivity according to the location of contacts in relation to the seizure onset zone while controlling for inter-electrode distance. Results For both adult and pediatric patients, resting connectivity was higher within compared to outside the seizure onset zone. However, resting connectivity between channels within and outside seizure onset zone was reduced. Stimulation connectivity followed a similar pattern, with elevated connectivity within the seizure onset zone but reduced connectivity from within to outside seizure onset zone. Significance These results support the hypothesis that the seizure onset zone is disconnected from the rest of the brain but intrinsically hyperconnected. This result helps reconcile prior inconsistencies across studies, aligns with basic science studies, and suggests an approach for future translational work aiming to localize the epileptogenic zone.

papers.title: Along-tract statistical mapping of white matter abnormalities in children with SeLECTS.
papers.authors: Xu G, Zhang Y, Huang K, Liu J, Song G, Chen X, Zeng L, Zhang Y, Liu H, Zhang T.
papers.abstract: Background and purpose Emerging evidence suggests that self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS) may reflect atypical neurodevelopment. As WM maturation extends from the second trimester through adolescence, this study aimed to identify regions of delayed or aberrant white matter (WM) development in children with SeLECTS using along-tract statistical mapping for precise localization of microstructural alterations. Materials and methods 38 children with SeLECTS and 31 healthy controls underwent diffusion-weighted MRI scan. Fractional anisotropy (FA), mean diffusivity (MD), and radial diffusivity (RD) were derived from the diffusion tensor model. Whole-brain tractography was performed using deterministic EuDX tracking and registered to a standardized bundle atlas in MNI space. Thirty WM tracts per subject were extracted. Linear mixed models within the BUAN tractometry framework were used to assess segment wise group differences, while partial correlations were performed to evaluate associations between diffusion metrics and cognitive performance. FDR correction was applied per bundle for all comparisons. Results After FDR correction, children with SeLECTS showed increased MD in the forceps minor, midbody of the corpus callosum, right corticospinal tract, right extreme capsule, and bilateral uncinate fasciculi. MD values in the affected WM segments showed negative correlations with performance and full-scale IQ, and the segments showing significant correlations overlapped with those showing significant group differences. Conclusions SeLECTS is associated with MD-based microstructural alterations in superficial frontal, temporal, and parietal pathways, potentially indicating delayed white matter maturation.

papers.title: Engineering composites inspired cortical-trabecular interlocking effect underlies bone strength in mouse vertebrae.
papers.authors: Mao R, Li Q, Yao J, Song C, Wang L, Fan Y.
papers.abstract: Bone strength is a major determinant of osteoporotic fracture risk. Current clinical assessments, however, rely primarily on imaging-based surrogates such as bone mineral density, offering limited insight into the integrated mechanical behavior of vertebral bone. Inspired by engineered composite structures, in which interfacial interactions substantially enhance mechanical properties, this study introduces the concept of the cortical-trabecular interlocking effect to characterize the mechanical integration between these two compartments and investigate its contribution to vertebral bone strength. Micro-finite element models of mouse L4 vertebrae (control, mild, and severe osteoporosis) and idealized vertebral models were employed to quantify the independent contributions of isolated cortical bone, isolated trabecular bone, and the cortical-trabecular interlocking effect to whole-bone mechanical properties under axial load. To better characterize the cortical-trabecular interlocking effect, we propose a novel microstructural parameter, Lr.BV/TV, defined as the bone volume fraction within the interlocking ring, an interface region where cortical and trabecular bone are structurally integrated. The cortical-trabecular interlocking effect contributed 12.2-26.1% (mean 19.5%) to vertebral yield strength and its magnitude varied systematically with osteoporosis severity. Notably, asynchronous deterioration of cortical and trabecular bone in osteoporosis constrained the effective utilization of the interlocking effect, whereas well-matched components maximized this effect. Lr.BV/TV was identified as the dominant predictor of vertebral strength and outperformed both cortical thickness and trabecular bone volume fraction, accounting for 45.83% of the total explained variance, with its predictive relevance varying across stages of osteoporosis. These findings advance our understanding of vertebral fragility.

papers.title: Neurovascular Coupling and Subclinical White Matter Alterations in Young Adults with Migraine without Aura: A Multimodal MRI and Machine Learning Study.
papers.authors: Chen Y, Kong Y, Zhang J, Wang H, Zhan S, Wang B, Tan W, Xu J.
papers.abstract: Rationale and objectives Young adults with migraine without aura (MwoA) may exhibit subtle white matter abnormalities, but their relationships with neurovascular measures, neurotransmitter distributions, and clinical burden remain unclear. We investigated these multimodal imaging associations in MwoA. Materials and methods A total of 130 patients with MwoA and 110 healthy controls (HCs) were enrolled. Multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was used to quantify white matter hyperintensity volume, free water (FW) fraction, peak width of skeletonized mean diffusivity (PSMD), and global neurovascular coupling (NVC); the regional measure was the cerebral blood flow (CBF)/fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (fALFF) ratio. Regional CBF/fALFF ratio alterations were spatially correlated with canonical neurotransmitter maps. Correlation, chain mediation, and machine-learning analyses were performed. Results Relative to HCs, patients with MwoA showed increased global FW fraction and PSMD and reduced global NVC. Decreased regional CBF/fALFF ratios involved sensorimotor, striatal, and cingulate regions. The spatial pattern of NVC abnormalities was positively associated with 5-HT1A, D1, DAT, and GABAergic maps, and negatively associated with D2 and noradrenaline transporter maps. FW fraction, PSMD, and regional CBF/fALFF ratio alterations were associated with migraine-related clinical indices. Random forest yielded the numerically highest area under the curve (0.866). Exploratory mediation analysis indicated that FW and PSMD statistically accounted for part of the association between regional CBF/fALFF ratios and clinical severity. Conclusion Young adults with MwoA exhibited subtle white matter microstructural abnormalities, reduced global NVC, and altered regional CBF/fALFF ratios. These cross-sectional findings suggest a potentially clinically relevant multimodal imaging pattern but require longitudinal and independent validation.

papers.title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Sequencing Identifies Altered Expression of Circadian Rhythm-Related Genes Pomc and Bmp4 in Post-Stroke Depression.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Li J, Yuan Y, Liu C, Luo D, Li Y, Chen W, Wu Z.
papers.abstract: Post-stroke depression (PSD) is a serious complication that significantly hinders stroke patients' recovery and quality of life. Uncovering the molecular changes that drive PSD is vital for understanding how depression develops following a stroke. In this study, we established a reproducible PSD model using minimally invasive photochemical-induced focal cortical lesion. Transcriptomic sequencing demonstrated that dysregulation of circadian entrainment genes is a central pathway in the development of post-stroke depressive-like behaviors. Protein-protein interaction network analysis of these circadian rhythm-related genes identified six hub genes. Four of these, including Pomc and Bmp4, exhibited expression patterns consistent with experimental validation. Integrated single-cell transcriptomic analysis further pinpointed cell-type-specific expression abnormalities of Pomc in endothelial cells and Bmp4 in oligodendrocytes. Subsequently, in silico perturbation analysis further indicated that their shared underlying regulatory mechanisms involve cell adhesion and extracellular matrix interaction. Collectively, using transcriptomic and single-cell sequencing in a PSD model, this study revealed altered expression patterns of circadian rhythm-related genes, providing potential targets for further investigation into the pathogenesis of PSD.

papers.title: Altered brain function and its spatial correlations with neurotransmitter maps in anterior shoulder pain patients.
papers.authors: Diao Z, Li H, Li Y, Liu C, Zheng Y, Lu J, Liu Y, Wei Z, Liu P, Qiao H.
papers.abstract: Neuroimaging studies have reported that chronic pain may be associated with brain functional changes and related molecular mechanisms. However, there are few studies in anterior shoulder pain (ASP). Thus, we aimed to assess the possible brain functional changes and their associations with neurotransmitter receptor maps in ASP patients. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data were obtained from 27 ASP patients and 20 healthy controls (HCs). Regional homogeneity (ReHo) and fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (fALFF) methods were used to examine altered brain functions. JuSpace toolbox was employed for evaluating the spatial correlations between ReHo and fALFF changes and neurotransmitter receptor maps. Regression analysis was conducted to explore the associations between neuroimaging findings and clinical characteristics in ASP patients. Furthermore, we investigated reliable biomarkers to distinguish ASP patients from HCs using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. ASP patients had abnormal ReHo/fALFF in the middle temporal gyrus, putamen, caudate, pallidum, precentral gyrus, medial prefrontal cortex, precuneus, posterior cingulate cortex and inferior temporal gyrus. ReHo/fALFF alterations in ASP patients were associated with the serotonin, dopamine, GABA, choline, glutamate and norepinephrine neurotransmitter systems. Visual analog scale was positively correlated with ReHo in the right insula. Moreover, ROC analysis showed higher classification accuracy in the middle temporal gyrus, precentral gyrus and putamen. Our study investigated abnormal brain function and associated neurotransmitter receptor maps in ASP patients, which may contribute to improving our understanding of the pathophysiological mechanisms in ASP.

papers.title: Bidirectional Regulatory Mechanisms of T cell-microglia Interactions in Cerebral Ischemic Disease: Molecular Crosstalk, Experimental Techniques and Therapeutic Implications.
papers.authors: Zheng Y, Cheng J, Li F, Ren Z, Chen C, Zhang Z, Lan X, Zhang C, Zhao Y, Han J, Li J, Cheng F, Wang Q, Li C, Wang X.
papers.abstract: Cerebral ischemic diseases, such as ischemic stroke (IS) and vascular dementia (VaD), are major causes of neurological disability and mortality. Neuroinflammation acts as a pivotal driver of secondary brain injury, mediated by intricate bidirectional interactions between peripheral T cells and central nervous system (CNS)-resident microglia. This review delineates the molecular mechanisms underlying T cell-microglia crosstalk in cerebral ischemia, emphasizing their dual roles in exacerbating neurotoxicity and promoting repair. Direct interactions involve antigen presentation via MHC-TCR engagement and co-stimulatory checkpoints (e.g., CD80/CD86-CD28, PD-L1-PD-1), which regulate T cell activation and microglial polarization. Direct signaling through cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-4, IL-17, IL-10) further modulates microglial phenotypes: Th1/Th17 cells drive pro-inflammatory M1 polarization via STAT1/NF-κB pathways, while Tregs/Th2 cells induce anti-inflammatory M2 states through STAT6/SMAD signaling. Spatial transcriptomics and single-cell omics reveal spatiotemporal dynamics of these interactions, identifying STAT1/STAT6 imbalance as a critical determinant of neuroinflammatory outcomes. Advanced methodologies, including two-photon intravital microscopy and microfluidic blood-brain barrier (BBB) models, enable real-time visualization of immune cell trafficking and synaptic communication. Therapeutically, targeting immune checkpoints (CTLA-4, PD-1) or cytokine pathways (e.g., IL-4 mimetics) shows promise in recalibrating neuroimmune responses. However, challenges such as blood-brain barrier impermeability to biologics and interspecies immune heterogeneity necessitate innovative delivery strategies. This review integrates molecular, cellular, and technological insights to propose a framework for precision immunomodulation. By elucidating context-dependent signaling nodes and leveraging emerging tools, the study underscores the potential of harnessing T cell-microglia crosstalk to mitigate neuroinflammation and enhance neural repair, offering transformative avenues for stroke and dementia therapy.

papers.title: Comment on "High-intensity interval training modulates APP expression and reduces neuronal apoptosis in a β-amyloid-induced model of Alzheimer's disease: hippocampal evidence".
papers.authors: Mello S, Zia I.
papers.abstract: Godinho et al. reported that high-intensity interval training (HIIT) modulated molecular and cellular markers associated with neuroprotection in a β-amyloid-induced model of Alzheimer's disease. However, the causal relationship between reduced APP expression and neuronal apoptosis, the translation of molecular adaptations into cognitive outcomes, and the discrepancy between FNDC5 mRNA and protein expression remain unclear. This Letter highlights these three considerations and discusses potential mechanisms that warrant further investigation.

papers.title: Human brain white matter charts in international populations
papers.authors: Huo Y, Zhang C, Ren F, Han T, Gao Y, Wang J, Ding J, Le L, Ou P, Bai T, Shen M, Feng G, Huang T, Li X, Chen Y, Jing R, Liu L, Tao S, Huang W, Cheng J, Su L, Zhang B, Xu Y, Ji G, Sun Y, Cao Q, Han Y, Ma G, He Y, Zuo X, Liu Y, Dong Q, Zhang Z, Shu N.
papers.abstract: Brain charts provide normative references for identifying neurodevelopmental milestones and clinically meaningful deviations. Existing white matter (WM) charts are derived predominantly from European and North American populations, limiting generalizability. Here, we established the first set of population-specific WM charts of 198 morphological and microstructural phenotypes for both Chinese (N=19,215) and Western (N=15,584) populations across the human lifespan. Developmental trajectories and spatial organization of WM maturation and degeneration were broadly conserved across the populations, whereas maturational timing varied across pathways and metrics. The Chinese population showed earlier maturation in several projection and sensorimotor pathways, but more protracted maturation in higher-order association and limbic pathways. Chinese population-matched charts more accurately predicted WM phenotypes and detected more extreme disease-related deviations in brain health in the Chinese population than Western-derived models. Individual deviation patterns further discriminated patients from healthy controls and predicted cognitive performance and plasma biomarkers. Our findings reveal population-specific WM maturation and show that reference-population mismatch can reduce the accuracy and clinical sensitivity of normative brain charts.

papers.title: Temporal modulation of cortical parvalbumin and somatostatin neurons shapes network activation and adaptation during microstimulation
papers.authors: Hughes CL, Kozai TD.
papers.abstract: Parvalbumin-positive (PV) and somatostatin-positive (SOM) inhibitory interneurons play distinct and critical roles in cortical sensory processing, yet their activation dynamics during patterned input remain unclear. This study used two-photon calcium imaging to measure how PV and SOM interneurons are activated and regulate layer 2/3 somatosensory cortical activity during prolonged, patterned input with 22 clinically relevant microstimulation patterns divided by temporal pattern (fixed, burst, or dynamic/biomimetic) and amplitude. Activation over time depended on the interaction between microstimulation amplitude, frequency, and duration. For fixed-frequency stimulation, PV neurons were generally more strongly activated than unlabeled neurons, while SOM neurons were more strongly engaged at higher amplitudes and frequencies, corresponding with greater suppression of surrounding populations over time. Burst patterns limited suppression by evoking stronger and more sustained activation than fixed-frequency patterns especially in PV neurons, potentially by reducing SOM feedback. Theta-burst stimulation (TBS) strongly activated and facilitated SOM neurons, which may underlie its therapeutic effects. Dynamic amplitude modulation preserved excitatory-inhibitory balance by eliciting brief, consistent responses that resemble natural sensory input while reducing long-term adaptation. Many findings fit a model in which PV provides fast-adapting feedforward inhibition and SOM provides slower-facilitating feedback. Supporting this model, distant PV neurons reached peak activation earlier than non-PV neurons, and SOM neurons later than non-SOM neurons during stimulation bursts. A simple computational model built on these dynamics reproduced observed responses, including distance-related effects. Neurons recruited directly bypass SOM input onto their dendrites leading to rapid PV-mediated depression but increasing activity across the stimulation pattern. Together, these results inform the design of microstimulation-based sensory restoration and clarify the circuit-level roles of PV and SOM neurons in transient and sustained inhibitory control of somatosensory cortex.

papers.title: Responses to unannounced rule changes in adults with developmental disabilities: A community-based pilot study with consumer-grade EEG
papers.authors: Jeong Y, Hyun S.
papers.abstract: Unannounced changes in rules or environments often precede challenging behavior and limit community participation for adults with developmental disabilities, yet their responses to change have rarely been quantified directly. We recruited adults with developmental disabilities, including those with intellectual disability, at a community day-service center. We administered a probabilistic reversal learning task and recorded resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) via a 14-channel wireless EEG system. Among the 12 adults who performed the task, total errors were comparable across participants (range 31–57), whereas a switch bias index, contrasting perseverative errors (persisting with the previously correct option) with regressive errors (failing to maintain the newly correct option), ranged from −0.96 to +0.91. In the 9 participants included in resting-state EEG analyses, a flatter aperiodic spectrum over the frontal cluster (preregistered, but selected as the focus post hoc) was associated with fewer switches after negative feedback (ρ = .80) and more perseverative errors (ρ = −.72). The preregistered parieto-occipital cluster showed the same direction (ρ = .69, 95% confidence interval [−.11, .97], n = 8), which was opposite to the preregistered prediction. Frontal alpha peak amplitude was associated with accuracy (ρ = .77), and the between-run reliability of resting-state measures was .82–.99. These findings provide preliminary evidence that EEG recorded in community settings can capture individual differences in how people respond to change. Field measurement that includes people with intellectual disability may help extend the evidence base for the Sustainable Development Goals of good health and well-being (SDG 3) and reduced inequalities (SDG 10).

papers.title: Convergent Mitochondrial and Oxidative Stress Signatures in Spaceflight and Tauopathy: A Comparative Multi-Omics Reanalysis in Drosophila melanogaster
papers.authors: Navarro M, Aquino J, Shi K, Lin H, Monfared V, Garcia JC, Seylani A, Komędera M, Moutinho J, Romils J, Venosa A, Kelam A, Bortolotto VC, Chen J, Gebre M, McNerney MW.
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a shared biological thread between terrestrial Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and in the unique stress environment of spaceflight, making mitochondrial pathophysiology a compelling target for comparative investigation. In AD, mitochondrial impairment is closely linked to defective oxidative phosphorylation, reactive oxygen species accumulation, calcium dysregulation, and neuronal injury, while spaceflight stressors such as microgravity and radiation disrupt mitochondrial homeostasis and increase oxidative stress. Understanding how the extreme stressors of spacelight affect mitochondrial function may provide insights into conserved mitochondrial stress responses and their implications for neurodegenerative diseases, including AD. Our study compares datasets from ground control Drosophila melanogaster RNA-seq with isolated radiation and microgravity exposure to discern conserved mitochondrial pathways and molecular signatures that may provide insights into AD mechanisms. Highlights Progressive mitochondrial upregulation observed from Earth to microgravity Tauopathy showed opposing downregulation of mitochondrial pathways Shared ETC and ATP synthesis pathways connect microgravity and Tauopathy Radiation induced minimal transcriptomic changes in spaceflight datasets Mitochondrial upregulation may reflect compensation in response to microgravity

papers.title: The Alzheimer’s disease risk gene ABCA7 regulates microglial lysosomal and lipid homeostasis and promotes phagocytosis to maintain neuronal health
papers.authors: Heuer SE, Ahsan FM, Terzioglu G, Misra A, Duong D, Katkar C, Giera M, van der Kant R, Seyfried NT, Young-Pearse TL.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Loss of function mutations in the lipid transporter ABCA7 have been linked to increased risk for late onset Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Although rare and common variants in ABCA7 associated with AD alter the coding sequence and are predicted to impair protein function, the precise cell-type consequences of ABCA7 deficiency remain incompletely defined. Methods We used CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing to generate induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) that were deficient for ABCA7 (ABCA7-KO) and their wild-type (ABCA7-WT) isogenic counterparts and subsequently performed unbiased proteomics on differentiated astrocytes (iAs), neurons (iNs) and microglia (iMGs). ABCA7 deficiency in iMGs produced the largest proteomic changes, so we therefore conducted additional functional analyses to define its effects on microglial lysosomal activity, phagocytosis, and lipid metabolism. In addition, we leveraged CRISPR/Cas9 to correct the ABCA7 rs3752246 AD risk variant in patient-derived iPSCs and compared proteomic and functional phenotypes between corrected iMGs and isogenic mutant carriers. Finally, we examined the functional consequence of ABCA7-deficient microglia on neurons. Results ABCA7-KO iMGs were deficient for proteins involved in lysosome function, measured by down-regulated lysosomal proteomic signatures, as well as reduced DQ-BSA activity and reduced LAMP1+ area. Additionally, ABCA7-KO iMGs displayed impaired phagocytic capacity and increased inflammatory markers, including MHC proteins CD1A and CD1E, and IL-18,. Multi-omic integration of lipidomic and proteomic profiles nominated a dysregulated metabolic network characterized by altered phospholipid steady-state metabolism and increased lipid peroxidation in ABCA7-KO iMGs. This was complemented by an accumulation of polyunsaturated triacylglycerols and lipid droplets, suggesting that ABCA7 deficiency disrupts intracellular lipid dynamics. This was supported by the alleviation of lysosomal and lipid droplet phenotypes through the inhibiting the synthesis of triacylglycerols. Concordantly, proteomic and functional analyses revealed lysosomal dysfunction in rs3752246-mutant iMGs, suggesting a shared ABCA7-dependent mechanism underlying AD risk. Tri-cultures of iNs, iAs and iMGs revealed that ABCA7 deficiency in iMGs worsened AD-relevant neuronal measures such as tau phosphorylation and synapse number. Conclusions This work supplies evidence for the important role of ABCA7 in microglia and provides unique insights into the molecular and functional consequences of reduced ABCA7 function in lysosomal and lipid regulation, paving a path forward to a more comprehensive understanding of AD molecular subtypes and personalized therapeutics.

papers.title: LATS2 modulates synaptic organization and function by regulating actin dynamics
papers.authors: Wigerius M, Labana PK, Diab A, Krueger S, Fawcett JP.
papers.abstract: Recent work has highlighted the importance of core Hippo pathway kinases in cycling cells. Many of these kinases are also expressed in post-mitotic neurons, where they have been linked to synaptic function, and more recently a number have been shown to be dysregulated in neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease. Despite this, little is known about the specific role or subcellular localization of the Large Tumor Suppressor kinases, LATS1 and LATS2, in postmitotic neurons. Previously, we demonstrated that LATS1 plays an important role in synapse development; however, the role of LATS2 remains poorly understood. Here, we examined the distribution and function of LATS2 and found that it is highly expressed in CA3/CA4 neurons of the hippocampus and localized throughout dendrites and dendritic spines. In contrast to LATS1, LATS2 expression remains stable throughout neuronal development. Furthermore, ectopic expression of LATS2 induces kinase-dependent structural spine defects, alters actin dynamics and reduces activity-dependent synaptic SEP-GluR1 fluorescence. Collectively, these findings reveal a unique distribution LATS2 in the hippocampus and demonstrate that LATS2 directly regulates actin dynamics and GluR1-containing AMPAR trafficking. Significance Statement The Hippo kinases LATS1 and LATS2 have been studied in proliferating cells, yet their function in post-mitotic neurons remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a distinct role for the LATS2 kinase in hippocampal neurons, where we find it is enriched in CA3/CA4 regions and localized to dendrites and dendritic spines. Unlike LATS1, we find LATS2 is maintained throughout neuronal maturation. We find LATS2 regulates dendritic spine structure, actin dynamics, and the trafficking of GLuR1-containing AMPA receptors in a kinase-dependent manner. These findings establish LATS2 as a novel regulator of synaptic structure and function and provide further evidence that Hippo pathway kinases play a role in synaptic morphology and function.

papers.title: Beyond Agrammatism: Syntax Processing in Chinese Primary Progressive Aphasia
papers.authors: Cheng Y, Chen T, Li-Ying LK, Lo RY, Tsoh J, Chan AL, Wong A, Mok VCT, Yan CT, Lu CJ, Sun Y, Wang P, Lee Y, Ng A, Leng F, Chen Y, Li C, Lin C, Chuang Y, Mandelli M, Gorno-Tempini ML, Tee BL.
papers.abstract: Syntax processing impairment is a defining feature of primary progressive aphasia (PPA), particularly in the nonfluent/agrammatic variant. However, current models are derived largely from Indo-European languages, and it remains unclear whether the cognitive and neuroanatomical mechanisms of syntax processing generalize to Chinese, an analytic, pro-drop language that encodes grammatical relationships primarily through word order and function words rather than inflectional morphology. Participants were recruited from the international Chinese Language Assessment in PPA cohort and included 64 individuals with PPA (19 logopenic, 15 nonfluent/agrammatic, 15 semantic, and 15 unclassifiable/mixed) and 60 cognitively healthy controls. Participants completed sentence comprehension and production tasks with systematically manipulated syntactic features. Item-level linguistic determinants were examined using ridge regression, diagnostic performance using receiver operating characteristic analyses, and neuroanatomical correlates using voxel-based morphometry of structural MRI. Performance on sentence comprehension and production was influenced by grammatical and lexical features. Subject-relative clauses, passive constructions, a higher proportion of function words, longer character length, and greater lexical content were associated with poorer performance among participants with PPA. Sentence comprehension was impaired in the logopenic, nonfluent/agrammatic, and semantic variants, even when isolated to the syntactic component of the sentence comprehension task. Similarly, sentence production was impaired across all PPA variants (all P < 0.01 versus controls). No significant differences were observed among PPA variants. Adjusted receiver operating characteristic analyses demonstrated high discrimination between each PPA variant and controls, with areas under the curve ranging from 0.87 to 0.97 for sentence comprehension-syntax and from 0.91 to 0.97 for sentence production. However, pairwise comparisons showed no significant differences in discriminative performance among PPA variants after correction for multiple comparisons. Both sentence comprehension-syntax and sentence production showed associations with semantic and repetition measures in addition to motor speech measures. Voxel-based morphometry showed that higher sentence comprehension-syntax scores were associated with greater grey matter volume in left frontotemporal and cingulate regions, whereas higher sentence production scores were additionally associated with greater gray matter volume in frontostriatal structures, including the caudate, putamen, and thalamus. Syntactic processing impairment in Chinese-speaking individuals with PPA extends beyond the nonfluent/agrammatic variant and is associated with distributed frontotemporal and frontostriatal regions, as well as lexical-semantic and auditory verbal short term memory mechanisms. These findings suggest that the cognitive and neural manifestations of syntactic impairment may be shaped by language-specific typological properties, underscoring the need for linguistically informed approaches to the assessment and interpretation of PPA.

papers.title: Identification of pleiotropic genes and biological mechanisms underlying the shared genetic component between asthma, neuropsychiatric disorders, and substance use behaviors
papers.authors: Huang H, Vernet R, Troubat L, Linhard C, Chataigner L, Suzuki Y, Fischer S, Aschard H, Demenais F, Bouzigon E, Julienne H.
papers.abstract: Asthma patients suffer from neuropsychiatric disorders (NPDs) more often than expected and NPD patients have a higher prevalence of smoking, which can lead to asthma. To investigate the genetic mechanisms underlying this complex relationship, we performed an integrative analysis of GWAS summary statistics from four asthma subtypes, 12 NPDs, and six substance use behaviors (SUBs). Asthma shares an important genetic component with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), major depressive disorder, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) that cannot be fully accounted for by smoking. Multi-trait GWAS identified 354 independent variants mapping to 178 pleiotropic genes capturing the core of the shared genetics of asthma, NPD, and SUB. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis across blood, brain, and lung tissues revealed pleiotropic gene overexpression in 57 cell types and three candidate mechanisms linking asthma and NPDs. First, immune-related pleiotropic genes are expressed in microglia, blood and lung immune cells, suggesting shared immune dysfunction. Second, the pleiotropic genes EP300 , RERE , and MAML3 regulate NOTCH signaling and are expressed in neurons, microglia, and lymphoid progenitors. Third, pleiotropic genes expressed in ciliated cells of both lung and brain implicate ciliary dysfunction. These findings may help identify new treatment strategies for patients with co-occurring asthma and neuropsychiatric disorders.

papers.title: Hidden Markov Modeling Reveals Altered Functional Network Dynamics in Multiple Sclerosis
papers.authors: Hiremath KC, Hobbs DA, Hettish DMR, Khan E, Alias BP, Lin MM, Fox PT, Chiang FL.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Purpose Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a neurodegenerative and demyelinating disease of the central nervous system. Recent evidence suggests that localized gray matter atrophy in MS may be involved in distributed functional brain networks. However, the dynamic trajectory of functional network alterations in MS remains unclear. The current study extends prior network-mediated findings and aims to investigate the dynamic functional connectivity (dFC) and energetic landscape across an atrophy-prone network in MS. Methods Twenty MS participants and twenty healthy controls (HC) underwent resting-state fMRI. The atrophy-based functional network (AFN) model was implemented, and time series from atrophy-prone regions were fit to a 12-state hidden Markov model. Each functional network state, a recurring pattern of activity across the AFN, was characterized by the AFN regions with the strongest activation. The states were then grouped into two metastates. Dynamic functional network metrics were compared between groups by permutation testing and correlated with disability and cognition. The energetic landscape of the network was mapped with a pairwise maximum-entropy model. Temporal irreversibility was also measured, which defines the arrow-of-time asymmetry of network dynamics. Results People with MS showed lower occupancy of state 1, which peaked on the right middle frontal and anterior cingulate cortex. Occupancy and mean lifetime were higher in states 3 and 10 (p < 0.05). In state 3, cortical activity was below the network average, and state 10 peaked on the postcentral gyrus. At the metastate level, MS participants spent more time in metastate M1 and less in M2 (p = 0.04). Within the MS group, a longer interval between visits to state 3 was associated with greater disability (r = 0.57), and a higher switching rate in state 10 with poorer verbal fluency (r = −0.50). The energetic landscape was similar between groups. Temporal irreversibility was lower in MS, mainly across subcortical connections. Conclusion MS participants dwelled longer in specific dFC states of the AFN, while the rate of transition between states did not differ from healthy controls. Dynamic functional network metrics were associated with disability and cognitive performance and may serve as functional correlates of clinical impairment. The states were similar between groups, whereas the directed drive between states was lower across subcortical connections. This pattern suggests altered network dynamics rather than altered network architecture in MS. Findings from this study characterize the functional network dynamics of neurodegeneration in MS, which may inform future development of network-based approaches for monitoring disease progression.

papers.title: Multiple Organ Dysfunction Trajectory Phenotypes After Severe Trauma Are Associated With Distinct Immune Profiles and Outcomes
papers.authors: Ding H, Cox M, Qiu Q, Mirabadi N, Bobrovnikov D, Gerbino K, Scherler K, Walters K, O’Keefe G, Brakenridge SC.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Traditional organ dysfunction classifications after severe trauma rely on binary categories (e.g., chronic critical illness [CCI] versus rapid recovery), which likely oversimplify the true heterogeneity of postinjury organ dysfunction trajectories and their underlying immune-biologic drivers. We hypothesized that severely injured trauma patients demonstrate multiple, distinct organ dysfunction phenotypes distinguished by unique immune signatures. METHODS We performed a prospective, longitudinal, observational cohort study of severely injured trauma patients at high risk for multiple organ dysfunction at a single Level 1 trauma center. Organ dysfunction was quantified daily through 28 days, death, or discharge using a trauma-specific modified Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (mSOFA) score excluding the neurologic subdomain to isolate systemic organ dysfunction from traumatic brain injury. We utilized group-based trajectory modeling to identify longitudinal mSOFA phenotypes. Plasma immune protein trajectories were compared across phenotypes using mixed-effects models with time interaction. RESULTS Sixty-nine patients were enrolled. Trajectory modeling identified five mSOFA phenotypes (c1-c5) with differences in resuscitation requirements, shock severity, and 28-day mortality, but not baseline demographics, injury severity, or early physiologic parameters. The phenotypes revealed organ dysfunction heterogeneity not fully captured by CCI/rapid recovery classification. Forty of 92 measured immune markers showed phenotype-differentiated trajectories (FDR<0.1). The most fulminant phenotype (c5) was distinguished by IL-17C, CXCL5, and CXCL6, implicating epithelial-barrier and neutrophil-trafficking mechanisms. The phenotype with highest CCI incidence (c3) was distinguished by rising CXCL9, ARTN, and TWEAK, implicating Th1 polarization and tissue-inflammation/repair signaling. The clinically distinct, older-age phenotype (c4) carried the largest differentiating signature (29 proteins), spanning renal injury/repair, endothelial activation, and adaptive lymphocyte modulation. CONCLUSIONS Organ dysfunction after severe trauma is more biologically heterogeneous than traditional clinical classifications suggest. Distinct mSOFA trajectory phenotypes correspond to distinct immune signatures, supporting separable pathobiology rather than a single axis of injury severity, with implications for phenotype-targeted precision immunomodulatory approaches in critical illness. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE Level III, Prognostic/Epidemiological.

papers.title: Spectral power and functional connectivity of resting EEG in people exposed to armed conflict and controls
papers.authors: Nitola Pulido L, Bonilla S, Herrera E, Reyes P, Santamaría-García H.
papers.abstract: Exposure to armed conflict can leave persistent effects on mental health, yet its neurophysiological correlates remain poorly characterized, particularly in populations exposed to prolonged violence outside narrowly defined post traumatic stress disorder samples. Here we examined resting state electroencephalographic activity in 122 Colombian adults, including 74 participants exposed to armed conflict and 48 controls. Eyes closed EEG was analysed for 240 seconds per participant. We quantified absolute and relative spectral power across delta, theta, alpha and beta bands and regional functional connectivity using weighted phase lag index in theta, alpha and beta. Group comparisons were adjusted for age, education, sex and assessment year, with correction across 78 EEG contrasts.
