In vitro, CK suppressed C1qA expression in BV2 cells and reduced synaptic C1qA deposition in HT22 cells. Conclusion CK ameliorated cognitive and synaptic deficits in APP/PS1 mice by inhibiting the C1qA/C3-CR3 pathway to suppress aberrant microglial synaptic phagocytosis and blocking NF-κB/NLRP3/GSDMD-mediated neuronal pyroptosis. These findings elucidate CK's neuroprotective mechanisms and provide scientific evidence for ginseng's traditional cognitive benefits.

papers.title: Mincle exacerbates neuroinflammation and dopaminergic neurodegeneration via synergistic crosstalk with TLR4.
papers.authors: Zhang W, Fu H, Shi W, Xue F.
papers.abstract: Microglial activation and subsequent neuroinflammation are critically implicated in the pathogenesis and progression of Parkinson's disease (PD). Macrophage-inducible C-type lectin (Mincle) is a pivotal pattern recognition receptor that participates in the regulation of innate immune responses. Nevertheless, the functional role of Mincle in mediating dopaminergic neuronal injury in PD remains poorly defined. In the present study, we observed a marked upregulation of Mincle expression in microglia in PD mouse models. Pharmacological inhibition of Mincle via Anti-Mincle antibody treatment effectively alleviated LPS-triggered dopaminergic neuronal loss in the SN and rescued motor behavioral impairments in mice. Additionally, Mincle blockade promoted microglial phenotypic transformation, driving a shift from the pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. Mechanistically, pharmacological blockade of either TLR4 or NF-κB signaling abrogated LPS-induced Mincle upregulation. Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assays further confirmed that the NF-κB/P65 subunit directly binds to the promoter region of the Mincle, verifying that the TLR4/NF-κB signaling serves as a critical upstream regulatory pathway for Mincle expression. Notably, this study provides the first in vivo evidence that Mincle activation by a Mincle-specific agonist trehalose-6,6-dibehenate (TDB) induces robust dopaminergic neurotoxicity and motor dysfunction in C57BL/6 J mice, accompanied by significant elevations in the expression of the pro-inflammatory and microglial activation markers iNOS and CD68. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that synergistic crosstalk between the Mincle-Syk signaling cascade and the TLR4/NF-κB pathway sustains the pro-inflammatory M1 microglial phenotype, thereby triggering progressive dopaminergic neuronal damage in the SN. This study uncovers a previously unrecognized pathogenic role of Mincle in neuroinflammation-mediated neurodegeneration, highlighting Mincle as a promising novel therapeutic target for PD intervention.

papers.title: A critical mechanistic synthesis of PINK1-mediated mitophagy signaling and its therapeutic targeting in Parkinson's disease neurodegeneration.
papers.authors: Khan A, Jawaid T, Rehman ZU, Alshammari MK, Bakht MA, Shakeel F, Zawiah M, Imran M.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that is associated with loss of dopaminergic neurons, mitochondrial dysfunction and disruption of cellular homeostasis. PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1) plays a crucial role in mitochondrial quality control by regulating mitophagy, mitochondrial dynamics, and calcium signaling to maintain neuronal bioenergetic homeostasis. This review critically evaluates the molecular pathways underlying PINK1-mediated mitochondrial integrity and the mechanisms by which loss-of-function mutations contribute to the pathogenesis of PD. Familial early-onset PD is strongly associated with pathogenic PINK1 mutations identified through genetic studies. Therapeutic approaches targeting the PINK1 pathway are examined, including adeno-associated virus (AAV)-based gene delivery, direct small-molecule PINK1 activation (MTK458), and indirect modulation of mitophagy and mitochondrial homeostasis by compounds such as curcumin, resveratrol, cannabidiol, gastrodin, and quercetin. Moreover, the complementary restoration of mitochondrial homeostasis through the modulation of downstream targets, such as transcription factor EB (TFEB) activation and BCL2-interacting protein 3-like (BNIP3L/NIX)-mediated mitophagy, is discussed as an indirect therapeutic strategy. Another important finding is that PD is a biologically and clinically heterogeneous disease that requires biomarker-directed and genotype-stratified therapeutic development. Finally, major translational issues are critically evaluated, including challenges related to blood-brain barrier penetration, target specificity, and long-term safety of mitochondrial modulators.

papers.title: Novel acylation modifications in cerebrovascular disease: Molecular mechanisms, crosstalk and therapeutic potential.
papers.authors: Yong Y, Liu T, Si M, Yang L, Bao X, Luo H, Chai C, Hua J.
papers.abstract: Secondary injury in cerebrovascular disease involves energy failure, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption and neurovascular unit dysfunction. Novel lysine acylations, including lactylation, succinylation, beta-hydroxybutyrylation and crotonylation, have emerged as interfaces through which metabolic changes in lactate, succinate, ketone bodies and short-chain acyl-CoA species are translated into transcriptional regulation and altered protein function. This review organizes the evidence according to a framework that links metabolic donors, writer and eraser enzymes, modification sites, cell types and disease stages. We distinguish relatively developed experimental evidence in acute ischemic stroke and cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury from limited findings in haemorrhage and predominantly exploratory evidence in chronic hypoperfusion and vascular cognitive impairment. Proteomic studies have identified 1003 lactylation sites across 469 proteins in rats subjected to cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury, although most sites have not undergone causal validation. Comparatively strong evidence has accumulated for sites or regulatory axes involving MeCP2, SOD2, NEK7, ACSL4, PLBD1 and ZO-1. Collectively, current findings indicate that the effects of a given acylation cannot be inferred from its global abundance because they depend on substrate function, cellular origin and the therapeutic window. Major limitations include insufficient site-specific causal evidence, difficulty in directly quantifying crosstalk among post-translational modifications, poor correspondence between animal models and clinical heterogeneity and the absence of effective delivery systems and pharmacodynamic biomarkers. Future studies should integrate spatiotemporally resolved multi-omics, endogenous site editing, cell-specific models, measurable target engagement and independent clinical cohorts to evaluate whether selected acylation sites can progress from experimental candidates to independently validated clinical markers or intervention targets.

papers.title: Design, synthesis, and pharmacological evaluation of 7-substituted 1,2,4-triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine derivatives as novel antiepileptic lead candidates targeting Nav1.2 channels.
papers.authors: He L, Zhang Q, Ma W, Qian M, Dong Y, Xin F, Guo C, Cao G, Tuo F, Huang L.
papers.abstract: The limitations of current antiepileptic drugs, including drug resistance and adverse effects, necessitate the development of novel therapeutic agents with improved efficacy and safety. Herein, we describe the design, synthesis, and pharmacological evaluation of a series of novel 1,2,4-triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine derivatives. Through strategic modification at the C-7 position, we identified compound 5m as a highly potent anticonvulsant agent. In the pentylenetetrazole (PTZ) epilepsy model, 5m exhibited exceptional antiseizure activity (ED50 = 8.84 mg/kg) with a high protective index (PI > 14.80), demonstrating superior efficacy and safety profiles compared to valproate, carbamazepine, and phenobarbital. Notably, 5m showed no neurotoxicity at its maximum soluble concentration. Preliminary structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis at the C-7 position suggested that the trifluoromethanesulfonate substituent, the pyrimidine nitrogen atoms, and the ortho-fluoro substitution pattern on the phenyl ring are important for potent activity. Mechanism of action studies combining electrophysiological patch-clamp recordings and molecular docking simulations established Nav1.2 channels as a primary molecular target, with 5m exhibiting inhibitory activity against Nav1.2 channels (23% ± 17% inhibition at 10 μM) and forming key interactions with residues LEU329, LEU336, ASN388, GLN391, and ARG395, while showing no significant effect on GABAA receptors. Furthermore, in silico ADMET prediction confirmed that 5m possesses excellent drug-like properties, including favorable gastrointestinal absorption and blood-brain barrier permeability, with no predicted toxicity. In summary, compound 5m represents a promising novel antiepileptic lead candidate with high efficacy, low neurotoxicity, and a favorable drug-like profile, warranting further preclinical development.

papers.title: Animal models for investigating post-stroke cognitive impairment: A neurovascular trafficking perspective.
papers.authors: Kaewkaen P.
papers.abstract: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is a major cause of long-term disability after ischemic stroke, yet its mechanisms remain incompletely explained by infarct volume, lesion location, or conventional vascular risk factors alone. Animal models are indispensable for clarifying how ischemic injury evolves into delayed cognitive dysfunction and for determining which mechanisms are experimentally tractable, reproducible, and translationally relevant. This review examines PSCI from a neurovascular trafficking perspective, focusing on how laboratory animal models can be used to investigate secretory pathway stress, endolysosomal dysfunction, autophagy-lysosomal flux, extracellular vesicle signaling, blood-brain barrier disruption, glial reactivity, myelin debris clearance, white matter injury, and cognition-relevant behavioral phenotypes. Rodent models of transient or permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion, photothrombotic stroke, embolic stroke, chronic cerebral hypoperfusion, bilateral carotid artery stenosis, and subcortical white-matter injury each reproduce selected components of the human PSCI spectrum. No single model fully captures the temporal, vascular, cellular, and cognitive complexity of human PSCI; therefore, model selection should be driven by the mechanistic question, disease phase, vascular pathology, cellular compartment, cognitive domain, and welfare burden under investigation. The central argument is not that neurovascular trafficking failure is already a proven causal pathway, but that well-designed animal studies can test, refine, or falsify this hypothesis. Future studies should integrate model validity, translational rigor, and welfare refinement through longitudinal cognitive testing, multimodal imaging, cell-specific molecular profiling, extracellular vesicle phenotyping, intervention-based validation, randomization, blinding, sample-size justification, humane endpoints, perioperative care, and transparent reporting.

papers.title: PBRM1 Deficiency in Microglia Leads to Excessive Neurogenesis and Autism-Like Behaviors via the CCL5-CCR1/5-β-catenin Signaling Axis.
papers.authors: Duan YY, Jiao LF, Liu PP, Duan CH, Li X, Zhang ZH, Zhang YQ, Ouyang XL, Du HZ, Liu S, Tang Y, Teng ZQ, Liu CM.
papers.abstract: The prevalence of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental disorder with limited effective therapeutic drugs, has been rising worldwide. Missense mutations in Polybromo 1 (Pbrm1), a core component of the SWI/SNF (switch/sucrose non-fermentable) chromatin remodeling complex, have been identified as a risk factor for ASD; however, whether PBRM1 loss of function contributes to the pathogenesis remains elusive. Here we provide direct evidence that microglial PBRM1 deficiency leads to altered microglial clusters, excessive neurogenesis, and ASD-like behaviors in mice. Integrated molecular analyses reveal that PBRM1 directly binds to the Ccl5 promoter and represses the expression of CCL5. Elevated CCL5 promotes the proliferation and neuronal differentiation of neural stem/progenitor cells (NSPCs) via the CCR1/5-β-catenin signaling pathway. Importantly, pharmacological blockade of CCR1/5 ameliorates behavioral deficits in Pbrm1 cKO mice. Together, these findings identify a previously unrecognized microglia-NSPC communication mechanism linking PBRM1 dysfunction to aberrant neurodevelopment and suggest the CCL5-CCR1/5 axis as a potential therapeutic target for ASD.

papers.title: Brain-thought states during movie-watching reflect shared sensory anchors and film- and person- specific processes in association cortex
papers.authors: Wallace RS, Hardikar S, Ketcheson S, Mulholland B, Goodall-Halliwell I, McKeown B, Chitiz L, Milham M, Xu T, Margulies DS, Ho N, Karapanagiotidis T, Poerio GL, Gonzalez Alam TRJ, Turnbull A, Skipper JI, Bernhardt BC, Leech R, Wammes JD, Jefferies E, Smallwood J.
papers.abstract: Naturalistic paradigms such as movie-watching have transformed functional neuroimaging by capturing cognitive dynamics during rich, real-world experiences. A fundamental challenge, however, is determining whether the neural signatures identified during these experiences reflect general principles of cognition or the specific contexts in which they are measured. To address this question, we combined fMRI data from participants watching eight diverse films with continuous reports of ongoing thought. We found that the generalizability of brain-thought relationships depends on the cognitive process being recruited. Neural signatures linked to sensory processing remained robust across films, whereas those involving memory-related association networks depended on how we modelled between-film variability, indicating that cognition becomes increasingly context-dependent along the cortical hierarchy from sensory to association cortex. Within default and limbic networks, we identified two contrasting memory-related states with opposite consequences for comprehension. One, reflecting the integration of prior knowledge with ongoing experience, predicted better narrative comprehension and was revealed only after accounting for between-film variability. The other, associated with stimulus-independent thought, predicted poorer comprehension and emerged only when between-film variability was not modelled. Together, these findings establish when brain-experience relationships measured during naturalistic paradigms can generalize across contexts and when they instead reflect interactions between cognition and the specific environments in which cognition unfolds. More broadly, the consistency of a given brain-experiential association may depend less on where it occurs in the brain and more on the viewer’s contextual experience: perceiving the film, drawing on memory to understand it, or drifting away. Significance statement Films have revolutionized how we study healthy and atypical brain activity by capturing synchronized, semi-unconstrained dynamics of real-world cognition. Yet experience is rarely measured alongside brain activity, and most studies use one or few films; thus, we do not know whether these neural and experiential responses generalize across films. By combining brain imaging with continuous reports of ongoing thought, we find a hierarchy: sensory processing is consistent across films, whereas memory-related processes in association cortex are uniquely sensitive to how film context is modelled. Two opposing memory states relate to comprehension. One draws on memory to support understanding; the other reflects stimulus-independent thought and impairs it. Identifying brain–experience relationships across films is crucial for developing and understanding naturalistic neuroscience.

papers.title: NeuroMark dFNC: Transferable Dynamic-State Templates for Subject-Specific and Frequency-Resolved Chronnectomics
papers.authors: Esfahani MM, Seraji M, Salem S, Jensen KM, Fu Z, Adali T, Wang Y, Calhoun V.
papers.abstract: Dynamic functional network connectivity (dFNC) commonly identifies recurring connectivity states from resting-state fMRI, but states derived independently in each dataset lack guaranteed correspondence across studies and cannot be directly estimated in new participants. We introduce NeuroMark dFNC, which extends the NeuroMark principle of prior-guided network estimation to dynamic connectivity by using reproducible reference states as priors for estimating corresponding subject-specific states. Reference-state templates were derived from UK Biobank using windowed functional network connectivity and time-frequency moments (TFMs), with split-sample reproducibility evaluated for k-means, independent component analysis (ICA), and principal component analysis (PCA) template-generation approaches. Constrained ICA then used the templates to estimate subject-specific state patterns and continuous loadings in independent FBIRN schizophrenia and ADNI Alzheimer's disease cohorts. ICA loadings were calibrated by their contribution to reconstruction of the original feature matrix. Fractional occupancy and conditional mean dwell time were calculated from the state with the largest absolute calibrated loading at each observation. The predefined templates avoided the need for dataset-specific state discovery and post-hoc state matching. In both clinical cohorts, the analysis identified state-dependent, distributed edgewise differences and differences in selected temporal summaries. Nominal frequency-resolved findings varied across states and moment-frequency bins and were treated as exploratory. NeuroMark dFNC provides a common state space for cross-cohort comparison while retaining subject-specific connectivity patterns and continuous state expression.

papers.title: Source-Decomposed Multimodal Graph Connectivity: A Temporal Mixture-Manifold Pipeline for Tracking Ischemic Injury and Treatment
papers.authors: Park H, Lee J, Nimmagadda A, Llinas B, Ghahfarokhi MF, Musto A, Ryu S.
papers.abstract: To capture the complex, dynamic network reorganization following acute focal brain injuries that standard static or unimodal neuroimaging frameworks routinely miss, we present an open, reproducible computational multimodal pipeline that integrates resting-state functional MRI and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) into dynamic, source-decomposed graph networks. This framework preserves sub-voxel, multi-peak distributional dynamics over time by modeling regional blood-oxygen-level-dependent signals within sliding windows using a Gaussian mixture model, with model complexity dynamically optimized. The resulting pairwise similarities define time-varying edge weights across local, nonlocal, and DTI-supported structural sources, unifying them into a multimodal connectivity manifold that precisely quantifies node strength, topological turnover, and boundary modifications. Applied to a non-human primate model of photothrombotic ischemia, the methodology revealed severe post-injury disruptions, with 66 of 144 nodes (45.8%) fundamentally altering their connectivity across localized sources. Furthermore, coupling this architecture with an Ensemble Kalman Filter (EnKF) allowed for the continuous tracking of a tissue “reversibility” coordinate, yielding earlier detection of metabolic state collapse than unimodal baselines and generating a forecast-divergence index as a rigorous early-warning signal. Extended across post-injury treatment boundaries to evaluate network recovery toward baseline, this interpretable, modality-aware framework establishes a standardized, shareable methodological foundation for tracking complex pathophysiological dynamics in neuroinformatics research.

papers.title: Local-Global Spherical Sliced Wasserstein Graph Kernel for Schizophrenia Identification.
papers.authors: Jia X, Chang X, Chang J, Jian Y, Dong D, Xu C.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of schizophrenia (SZ) using functional connectivity (FC) is fundamentally challenged by the non-Euclidean geometry of neuroimaging data and information loss from arbitrary graph thresholding. To overcome these bottlenecks, this study proposes the local-global spherical sliced Wasserstein graph (LG-SSWG) kernel. By embedding FC profiles onto a hyperspherical manifold, the proposed framework utilizes geodesic optimal transport to construct a mathematically rigorous, positive-definite graph kernel. This threshold-free approach synergistically integrates macroscopic whole-brain topology and region-specific functional architectures. Evaluated on the public COBRE dataset, LG-SSWG achieves a superior 84% accuracy, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. Beyond predictive accuracy, the method exhibits strong clinical interpretability by identifying critical neuroanatomical biomarkers, particularly the left thalamus and right precuneus. Network analysis reveals pervasive functional hyperconnectivity within subcortical relays and cognitive networks in SZ patients. Notably, this hyperconnectivity correlates positively with PANSS positive symptom scores. Consequently, these altered thalamocortical and precuneus-anchored circuits indicate that SZ clinical symptoms may be closely associated with disrupted sensory gating and functional segregation. Ultimately, the LG-SSWG kernel provides a principled geometric learning tool that advances both the objective diagnosis and mechanistic understanding of schizophrenia.

papers.title: Sublexical compensatory reorganization of Chinese character recognition in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.authors: Liu B.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical and experimental neuropsychology
papers.abstract: Objective This study investigated the cognitive-functional shift in visual character recognition across the cognitive decline trajectory, ranging from healthy aging through Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) to Mild Alzheimer's Disease (AD). Specifically, it was hypothesized that as global semantic networks degrade, the reliance on rapid holistic processing decreases, prompting a compensatory shift toward sublexical features. Method Using a controlled unmasked priming lexical decision paradigm, this study evaluated behavioral performance across three distinct participant groups (N = 30 per group): healthy controls (HC), individuals with MCI, and patients with Mild AD. The experimental stimuli consisted of 80 Chinese phonograms matched across key psycholinguistic properties. This study utilized mixed-design Analyses of Variance (ANOVAs) alongside item-level hierarchical multiple regression (HMR) models to isolate the specific drivers of reaction times, assessing the predictive power of visual complexity, whole-character frequency, semantic transparency, and phonetic regularity. Results The analytical models revealed distinctly divergent psycholinguistic trajectories. The HC group demonstrated highly efficient holistic processing, with performance primarily driven by whole-character frequency. Conversely, the MCI group exhibited a unique transitional cognitive profile, characterized by a simultaneous reliance on both holistic whole-word access and analytic sublexical features. Crucially, in the Mild AD tgroup, the holistic processing advantage was entirely abolished. This functional disintegration triggered a compensatory reorganization toward bottom-up sublexical properties, with patients relying heavily on semantic transparency and phonetic regularity to achieve semantic access. Conclusions These findings demonstrate a linguistic Compensation-Related Utilization of Neural Circuits Hypothesis (CRUNCH) effect within the degenerating brain. As top-down lexical-semantic hubs deteriorate, reflected behaviorally in this paradigm by the loss of holistic processing advantages, the cognitive system actively compensates by upregulating bottom-up, sublexical pathways. Furthermore, the transitional sublexical dependency observed during the MCI stage highlights the translational potential of psycholinguistic variables as sensitive, noninvasive behavioral biomarkers for the early screening and monitoring of dementia.

papers.title: A microglial basis for fragile X syndrome via impairment of FMRP-regulated lysosomal function.
papers.authors: Li H, Choi JJ, Huang EJ, Xu B.
papers.abstract: Silencing of the FMRP-encoding FMR1 gene results in fragile X syndrome (FXS), the most common inheritable intellectual disability and autism. FMRP regulates various neuronal functions but clinical trials targeting neurons have failed, suggesting unrecognized disease mechanisms. We find that mice with selective Fmr1 deletion in microglia exhibit audiogenic seizures (AGS) and parvalbumin (PV) neuron loss, recapitulating two key phenotypes observed in FXS (Fmr1-/y ) mice. By combining snRNA-Seq and RNA immunoprecipitation, we identify several lysosomal mRNAs as FMRP binding targets. FMRP promotes lysosomal protein expression and its deficiency disrupts lysosomal function in microglia. Notably, FMRP depletion reduces Grn-encoded secretory progranulin and increases PV neuron apoptosis in immature brains. PV neuron density is decreased similarly in Grn+/- , Fmr1-/y , and Grn+/- ;Fmr1-/y mice, and progranulin overexpression rescues AGS and PV neuron loss in Fmr1-/y mice. Thus, our study identifies microglia and progranulin as critical regulators of FXS pathogenesis and potential targets for FXS therapy.

papers.title: Cholinergic-dependent metaplasticity in the amygdala-insula pathway during incubation of cocaine craving.
papers.authors: Salin A, Lardeux V, Dugast E, Balado E, Thiriet N, Jaber M, Solinas M, Belujon P.
papers.abstract: The time-dependent increase in drug seeking during abstinence, termed 'incubation of craving' is believed to play a major role in the persistent risks of relapse. This phenomenon is associated with synaptic plasticity changes across brain structures involved in reward processing, executive functions, emotion regulation and inhibitory control. The basolateral amygdala (BLA) and the anterior insular cortex (aIC) are two interconnected structures involved in processing internal and external drug-related cues and are known to play a role in drug craving. However, whether chronic cocaine alters synaptic plasticity within the BLA-aIC circuit and how these changes evolve during abstinence remains unclear. Here, using cocaine self-administration and in vivo electrophysiological recordings in anesthetized male rats, we demonstrate that, while long-term potentiation in the BLA-aIC pathway remains intact, long-term depression is disrupted throughout abstinence in both cocaine- and sucrose-rats, indicating a persistent impairment in synaptic weakening mechanisms. Importantly, a loss of depotentiation was observed after late but not early abstinence, and was specific to cocaine self-administration, identifying it as a hallmark of incubation of craving. Systemic, but not local intra-aIC, blockade of muscarinic receptors with atropine restored depotentiation and reduced cocaine-seeking behavior. Finally, qPCR analysis revealed region-specific transcriptional adaptations, with upregulation of muscarinic, NMDA and AMPA receptor transcripts in the BLA and a selective decrease of Grin2a in the aIC. Together, these findings point to cholinergic regulation of BLA-aIC metaplasticity as a candidate mechanism underlying incubation of cocaine craving.

papers.title: zDHHC11 is a common palmitoyltransferase regulating microglia-mediated neuroinflammation across neurodegenerative diseases.
papers.authors: Luo H, Jiang D, Hao Z, Bu J, Wang J, Xu N, Nie X, Zhang Y, Yin Q, Zhuang P.
papers.abstract: Purpose Microglia-mediated neuroinflammation is a shared feature across Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and diabetic cognitive impairment (DCI), but the convergent molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated whether protein S-palmitoylation serves as a common regulator of microglial neuroinflammation across distinct neurodegenerative diseases etiologies and aimed to identify the key palmitoyltransferase involved. Methods In vivo ND models (APP/PS1 for AD, MPTP for PD, STZ/high-fat diet for DCI) and in vitro BV2 microglial models stimulated with amyloid-β (Aβ), lipopolysaccharide (LPS), or high glucose (HG) were established. Microglial morphology, inflammatory responses, and the TLR4/MyD88 pathway were assessed by immunofluorescence, RNA-seq, RT-qPCR, and ELISA. Protein palmitoylation levels were evaluated using 2-BP and ABE assays. Palmitoyltransferase expression profiling was performed, and protein-level validation was conducted both in vitro and in vivo. Subsequently, the identified common enzyme, zDHHC11, was knocked down by siRNA to determine its functional role. Results All three ND models showed robust microglial activation with a pro-inflammatory amoeboid morphology. Aβ, LPS, and HG each upregulated pro-inflammatory cytokines and activated the TLR4/MyD88 pathway in BV2 cells. Palmitoylation inhibition with 2-BP attenuated cytokine production, and all three stimuli increased total protein palmitoylation. Among all palmitoyltransferases screened, zDHHC11 was uniquely and consistently upregulated by all three stimuli. This upregulation was further corroborated at the protein level, with elevated zDHHC11 expression observed both in cultured cells and in brain tissue sections. Knockdown of Zdhhc11 suppressed cytokine expression/secretion and reduced TLR4/MyD88 levels, indicating that zDHHC11 acts upstream of this common pathway. Conclusion Protein S-palmitoylation mediated by zDHHC11 is a convergent mechanism driving microglial pro-inflammatory activation across distinct ND etiologies. zDHHC11 represents a common regulator of TLR4/MyD88-dependent neuroinflammation and a potential therapeutic target for multiple NDs.

papers.title: Ziziphora clinopodioides Flavonoids exerts neuroprotective effects through PI3K/Akt pathway to improve ischemic stroke.
papers.authors: Zhuo X, Li S, Zhang W, Deng M, Shan X, Ding S, Zhang X, Shatewalede T, Yang W, Gu L, Li Q.
papers.abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance Ziziphora clinopodioides Lam. is a traditional Uyghur medicinal herb used for centuries in Xinjiang, China, to treat cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disorders. According to local ethnopharmacological records, it is traditionally employed to promote blood circulation, remove blood stasis, calm the heart, and relieve chest tightness and palpitations. Modern studies have shown that its total flavonoids (ZCF) possess anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. Ischemic stroke (IS) is a leading cause of death and disability, involving neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption. However, the neuroprotective mechanism of ZCF against IS and its active constituents remain unclear. Aim of the study This study aimed to elucidate the neuroprotective mechanism of ZCF against IS and to identify its potential active flavonoids. Materials and methods Network pharmacology and transcriptomics were used to predict core pathways, followed by in vitro and in vivo experiments. Neurological deficits, infarct volume, BBB integrity, and PI3K/Akt-related inflammatory/oxidative markers were assessed. The PI3K inhibitor LY294002 was used, and active flavonoids were screened by molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and ELISA. Results Integrated transcriptomics and network pharmacology identified that ZCF modulates the PI3K/Akt pathway. In MCAO/R-treated rats, ZCF reduced cerebral infarction, and preserved neuronal morphology. ZCF protected BBB integrity by restoring ZO-1, Occludin, Claudin-5, reducing MMP-9 and MMP-2 levels, rebalancing the Ang-1/Ang-2 ratio, decreasing NaF permeability, and increasing TEER. ZCF activated PI3K/Akt signaling in both bEnd.3 cells and MCAO/R-treated rat brain tissues, and the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 reversed ZCF-mediated regulation of tight junction proteins, matrix metalloproteinases, and Ang-1/Ang-2, suggesting that ZCF preserves BBB integrity at least partly through a PI3K/Akt-dependent mechanism. ZCF inhibited the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 axis, reduced IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α and MDA, and up-regulated Nrf2 and SOD, and these effects were reversed by LY294002. Molecular docking and MD simulations suggested that Diosmin, Glycitin, and Tilianin may form stable binding with PI3K. Diosmin, Glycitin and Tilianin could significantly restore the activity of PI3K in PC12 cells treated with OGD/R, reduce the levels of IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α and MDA, and enhance the activity of SOD. Conclusion Under preconditioning conditions, ZCF maintains BBB and inhibits neuroinflammation and oxidative stress through integrity and PI3K/Akt dependence, thereby exerting anti-IS protection. Diosmin, Glycitin, and Tilianin are potential active flavonoids that may contribute to PI3K/Akt activation.

papers.title: Altered resting-state EEG microstate dynamics are associated with auditory hallucinations in patients with major depressive disorder.
papers.authors: He Y, Wu F, Liao F, Zhang Z, Wu J, Zhang X, Li H, Wu K, Zhao Y, Wang L, Huang Y.
papers.abstract: Background Auditory hallucination experiences are an understudied but clinically significant feature of major depressive disorder (MDD). Although EEG microstate abnormalities have been reported in MDD, their relationship with auditory hallucination experiences remains unclear. This study investigated resting-state EEG microstate dynamics associated with auditory hallucination experiences in first-episode MDD. Methods A total of 182 first-episode patients with MDD and 95 healthy controls underwent resting-state EEG recordings. Patients were classified according to lifetime history of auditory hallucination experiences into those with (AH+, n = 42) and without (AH-, n = 140) such experiences. Patients were either psychotropic medication-naïve or minimally medicated (<2 weeks of cumulative exposure). Microstate parameters were compared among groups. ANCOVA and hierarchical binary logistic regression were performed to examine associations with auditory hallucination experiences. Results Only microstate C occurrence was significantly higher in the AH+ group than in both the AH- and healthy control groups after multiple-comparison correction. This difference remained significant after adjustment for age, sex, education, and depression severity. Hierarchical logistic regression showed that higher microstate C occurrence was independently associated with auditory hallucination experiences (OR = 1.773, 95% CI: 1.211-2.595, p = 0.003), but not with hallucination severity. Its discriminatory ability was modest (AUC = 0.614, 95% CI: 0.516-0.711). Conclusions In first-episode MDD, a lifetime history of auditory hallucination experiences was associated with increased microstate C occurrence. This finding suggests that altered microstate C dynamics may represent an electrophysiological correlate of auditory hallucination experiences, warranting further investigation.

papers.title: Post-traumatic epilepsy: An historical review from ancient observations to modern molecular mechanisms.
papers.authors: Churn SB.
papers.abstract: Post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE) represents a significant neurological complication of traumatic brain injury (TBI), accounting for approximately 5% of all epilepsies and 10-20% of structural/symptomatic epilepsies in population studies. This review traces the evolution of PTE research from ancient medical observations through 140+ years of modern scientific investigation, with emphasis on the historical, epidemiological and clinical-trial literature that established the field's current conceptual and diagnostic framework. Molecular and cellular mechanisms are introduced only briefly as a bridge to this historical narrative, as they are addressed in-depth elsewhere in this special issue. Thus, this review will focus upon the transition from purely observational studies in the late 19th century through epidemiological investigations of wartime injuries, the development of animal models, molecular mechanistic discoveries, and contemporary prevention trials. Recent meta-analytic data (2022-2025) indicate that modern-era severe TBI cohorts show higher long-term PTE incidence than older estimates suggested. Despite substantial progress, PTE remains largely unpreventable, representing a critical unmet medical need, though a maturing pipeline of biomarker-enriched antiepileptogenesis trials offers genuine hope for the coming decade.

papers.title: Contralateral piriform cortex alterations after surgery for temporal lobe epilepsy: A pilot MRI volumetry study.
papers.authors: Pek G, Ünal S, Doğan İ, Erdoğan S.
papers.abstract: Purpose Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is increasingly conceptualized as a network disorder, with the piriform cortex as an implicated region. We characterized postoperative contralateral piriform cortex-cortical amygdala (PCA) structural and perfusion-related changes in a small seizure-free TLE cohort. Methods Nine patients with drug-resistant TLE who underwent epilepsy surgery and achieved postoperative seizure freedom were included in this single-center pre-post pilot study. Bilateral PCA was manually delineated on 3D T1-weighted MRI using ITK-SNAP, and volumes were normalized to total intracranial volume derived from CAT12 segmentation. Eight atlas-derived contralateral temporal lobe regions were examined as exploratory regional-specificity comparisons. In patients with available pulsed arterial spin labeling (PASL), piriform and putaminal signal intensities were measured by region-of-interest analysis. Non-parametric paired tests were used; secondary and exploratory analyses were corrected using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure. Results Normalized to total intracranial volume (TIV) contralateral PCA volume decreased postoperatively (Wilcoxon Z = -2.073, exact two-tailed p = 0.039; r = 0.69). None of the eight atlas-derived contralateral temporal regions showed a significant pre-post volume change. Contralateral putamen-normalized piriform signal intensity did not change significantly (Z = -0.105, p = 0.917), and no secondary or exploratory analysis remained significant after FDR correction. Conclusions In this hypothesis-generating pilot cohort, contralateral PCA volume decreased after epilepsy surgery, whereas the PASL-derived signal-intensity measure did not show a corresponding group-level change. These observations do not establish a surgery-induced network mechanism and require confirmation in larger controlled longitudinal cohorts.

papers.title: Potential Mechanisms of N-Methyltyramine in Multitarget Regulation of Mental Disorders via the GPCR-cAMP Pathway.
papers.authors: Zijian W.
papers.abstract: N-Methyltyramine (NMT) is a tyramine derivative widely distributed in citrus plants and the traditional Chinese medicine Zhishi. Pharmacological studies have confirmed that NMT directly binds to the dopamine D₂ receptor (DRD2; Ki = 31.3µM), inhibits forskolin-induced cAMP accumulation (EC₅₀ ≈ 4µM, Emax = 89%), and dose-dependently antagonizes quinpirole-mediated β-arrestin2 recruitment, exhibiting G protein-biased agonistic properties. Meanwhile, NMT activates the human trace amine-associated receptor 1 (hTAAR1; EC₅₀ ≈ 2µM) to increase cAMP, possesses α₂-adrenergic receptor antagonistic activity (IC₅₀ = 5.53µM), and exhibits blood-brain barrier permeability (logPe = -5.16cm/s). Based on these multi-target receptor profiles, NMT may participate in the regulation of central monoaminergic neurotransmission via the GPCR-cAMP signaling axis, providing a new multi-target lead compound direction for research on neurological disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, depression, and drug addiction. Notably, evidence for direct activation of β₂-adrenergic receptors by NMT remains insufficient, and its therapeutic effects and downstream signal integration mechanisms require NMT-specific experimental validation.

papers.title: MRI-based correlation of cry acoustic parameters and brain structural development in preterm infants.
papers.authors: Zhu X, Cao Q, Xu F, Duan Y, Huang M, Hua Z.
papers.abstract: Objective Infant crying conveys abundant information, including neurophysiological, pathological, and psychological aspects. However, the relationship between crying and brain structure remains poorly understood. Methods In this study, 154 preterm infants and 84 term infants were enrolled, and their cries were recorded for 1 min under similar stimulation conditions. MATLAB software was used to analyse the crying data, for statistical analyses, repeated cry-level observations were averaged within infant, and each infant contributed one value for each cry acoustic parameter. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was performed in 43 preterm infants to measure the volumes of grey matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Results Preterm infants had longer cry cycle and inhale durations than term infants (P = 0.022 and 0.014). Among preterm infants, cry parameters did not differ significantly across gestational ages (all P > 0.05). In 43 preterm infants with MRI, grey and white matter volumes differed significantly across gestational age groups (P = 0.01 and 0.02), as did the grey matter/CSF and white matter/CSF ratios (P = 0.010 and 0.020). Correlations between cry parameters and brain volumes were generally weak. Multiple linear regression showed that cry parameters were associated with white matter volume (R2 = 0.38, P = 0.039) but not with grey matter or CSF volume. Conclusion This study identified associations between cry characteristics and MRI-derived brain volumes in infants across gestational ages. Although these findings suggest that cry characteristics may reflect certain aspects of brain development, the observed associations were generally weak and should be considered exploratory.

papers.title: MRI and proton MR spectroscopy in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy: a comprehensive imaging review.
papers.authors: Enokizono M.
papers.abstract: Neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) remains a leading cause of neonatal mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental disability. Although cranial ultrasound is widely used as a bedside screening tool, brain MRI has become central to diagnosis, injury pattern classification, timing estimation, and outcome prediction. Furthermore, proton MR spectroscopy (1 H-MRS) provides complementary metabolic biomarkers that enhance prognostication. This review focuses on MRI and 1 H-MRS in neonatal encephalopathy due to hypoxic-ischemic injury, addressing both term and preterm infants. The pathophysiologic determinants of injury distribution are summarized, the optimal timing of imaging and diffusion evolution is discussed, and practical acquisition protocols including recommended sequences and 1 H-MRS parameters are proposed. Key MRI phenotypes in term infants-basal ganglia-thalamus injury, watershed/parasagittal cortical-subcortical injury, and global or near-total injury patterns are reviewed with attention to common pitfalls such as diffusion pseudonormalization and evolving T1/T2 signal changes. For preterm infants, this review highlights distinctive vulnerabilities of the germinal matrix and periventricular white matter, emphasizing the spectrum from punctate white matter injury (WMI) to cystic periventricular leukomalacia (PVL). For 1 H-MRS, voxel selection, echo time considerations, and interpretation of lactate, N-acetylaspartate (NAA), choline, creatine, and myo-inositol are detailed. Evidence suggests that deep gray matter lactate/NAA or NAA-based metrics serve as reliable and robust outcome biomarkers. Emerging directions including arterial spin labeling (ASL) perfusion are also discussed.

papers.title: Anatomical and radiological analysis of ventricular catheter trajectories: neuronavigation-guided dissection and tractography-based 3D visualization.
papers.authors: Kara CF, Akyüz ME, Elveren M, Temtek U, Zeynal M, Kapakin S, Yalçın A, Gök E, Kadıoğlu HH, Şahin MH.
papers.abstract: Ventricular catheter placement (VCP) is a life-saving intervention frequently performed in emergency departments and intensive care units. The free hand technique is the most commonly used approach for placing catheters. This study demonstrates the anatomical and radiological relationship between catheters inserted through the most commonly used access points and the anatomical structures in their path. Moreover, we calculate the insertion angles and catheter lengths that should be specified during VCP. Six donated human heads, fixed in 10% formalin and injected with colored silicone dye, were used in this study. Ventricular catheters were inserted through Kocher's, Paine's, Keen's, Frazier's, and Dandy's points under navigation. Dissection was performed from the skin to the inner wall of the ventricle while preserving the inserted catheters. The insertion angle and delivery length for each access point were measured both in the donated human heads and in 50 patients with hydrocephalus. In addition, magnetic resonance tractography was performed, and the relationship of each catheter with anatomical structures was presented as a three-dimensional model. Catheters inserted from Keen's and Paine's points pass through regions containing dense and crucial vascular structures. Catheters inserted from Keen's, Paine's, and Frazier's points enter the cortex through eloquent areas. The catheter inserted from Keen's point passes through the most diverse white matter pathway. Catheters inserted from Kocher's and Dandy's points pass through regions with less dense cortical vascular structures. Moreover, they pass through noneloquent cortical structures and fewer white matter tracts. This is the first anatomical dissection and tractography report describing the relationship between catheters introduced through the most common ventricular access sites and the anatomical structures along their path from the skin to the ventricle. Understanding the anatomical and radiological three-dimensionality of VCP will increase the safety of its applications.

papers.title: miR‑660‑5p ameliorates neuronal damage in Alzheimer's disease via targeting APP.
papers.authors: Gong P, Su X, Fang Y.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder of the central nervous system. To investigate miR‑660‑5p expression among patients with AD and explore the molecular mechanism underlying its regulation of AD‑related pathological progression. A total of 86 AD patients and 86 healthy controls were enrolled. Serum miR‑660‑5p was detected by real‑time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). Inflammatory factors were measured via enzyme‑linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). SH‑SY5Y cells were treated with aggregated Aβ₁‑₄₂ preparation to establish an in‑vitro AD‑like injury model. Serum miR‑660‑5p was significantly downregulated in AD patients (P < 0.001), positively correlated with Mini‑Mental State Examination (MMSE, r = 0.684) and Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA, r = 0.640) scores, and negatively correlated with serum interleukin‑6 (IL‑6, r = - 0.658) and tumor necrosis factor‑α (TNF‑α, r = - 0.614). Receiver‑operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis for AD yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.873. Mechanistically, miR‑660‑5p targets and inhibits APP expression to mitigate Aβ‑induced neuronal injury and neuroinflammation. miR-660-5p is downregulated in patients with AD. It mitigates aggregated Aβ₁-₄₂ preparation‑triggered neuronal damage and neuroinflammation in vitro by targeted inhibition of APP expression.

papers.title: Altered resting-state functional connectivity in lung cancer patients with comorbid depressive symptoms.
papers.authors: Zhou H, Tang W, Ren H, Li K, Ren N, Li R, Duan J, Wang D, Zhang H, Tan F, Zhang X.
papers.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
papers.abstract: Background It is quite common clinically for cancer patients (including those with lung cancer) to have comorbid depressive symptoms. Numerous studies have shown that patients with depression often have altered resting-state functional connectivity (RS-FC). However, only a few studies have reported abnormal RS-FC in cancer patients with comorbid depressive symptoms. This exploratory and cross-sectional study examined a heterogeneously treated Chinese lung cancer population. Data on psychotropic medication, cancer-related symptoms, and detailed treatment histories were not systematically collected. The main objective was to observe the relationship between comorbid depressive symptoms and RS-FC in this population, which has not been reported yet. Methods We calculated whole-brain RS-FC in 33 lung cancer patients with comorbid depressive symptoms and 42 age- and sex-matched lung cancer patients without comorbid depressive symptoms. The Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) was used to assess depressive symptoms in lung cancer patients. Results Compared to lung cancer patients without depressive symptoms, those with comorbid depressive symptoms showed altered RS-FC across eight brain region pairs: (1) left calcarine cortex-right cerebellar lobules IV-V, (2) left medial frontal gyrus-left anterior cingulate gyrus, (3) left insular-left middle temporal gyrus, (4) left precentral gyrus-left cerebellar lobule Ⅲ, (5) left thalamus-vermis Ⅰ and Ⅱ, (6) right olfactory cortex-right fusiform gyrus, (7) right rectus gyrus-right cerebellar lobule Ⅶ b, and (8) right cerebellar lobule Ⅶ b and right olfactory. Furthermore, total depressive symptom scores were negatively correlated with RS-FC between multiple brain regions, including the left superior frontal gyrus and right middle temporal gyrus (r = -0.72, p < 0.001), left superior frontal gyrus and left temporal pole middle temporal gyrus (r = -0.69, p < 0.001), left triangular inferior frontal gyrus and left temporal pole middle temporal gyrus (r = -0.65, p < 0.001), left medial superior frontal gyrus and right middle temporal gyrus (r = -0.65, p < 0.001), left insula and right cerebellar crus II (r = -0.6, p < 0.001), and right superior temporal gyrus and right cerebellar crus II (r = -0.67, p < 0.001). Conclusions Our findings suggest preliminary associations between depressive symptoms and altered RS-FC in lung cancer patients, with connectivity changes correlating with symptom severity. However, because data on psychotropic medication use, cancer-related symptoms (e.g., pain, fatigue), and treatment details were not systematically collected, these findings should be considered preliminary and hypothesis-generating rather than definitive markers of comorbid depression. Future longitudinal studies with systematic assessment of medication, treatment, and multidimensional symptom burden are needed to determine whether these connectivity patterns specifically reflect depressive symptoms or broader cancer-related sequelae.

papers.title: Facial emotion recognition of sadness relates to superior parietal gray matter volume in mild cognitive impairment.
papers.authors: Mahadevan R, Giesers NK, Liman T, Witt K, Hildebrandt A, Roheger M, Rosemann S.
papers.abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is associated with early, regionally selective neurodegenerative changes that may affect socioemotional functioning before atrophy becomes widespread. This study examined whether structural brain alterations in MCI relate to facial emotion recognition performance. Sixty adults (30 MCI, 30 healthy controls), aged 50-86 years, completed neuropsychological testing, the Facial emotion composite Task, and structural MRI. Whole-brain voxel-based morphometry revealed no significant gray matter volume differences between groups. However, targeted region-of-interest ROI analyses demonstrated lower right amygdala and bilateral hippocampal volumes in patients with MCI. Cortical thickness analyses identified two regions with lower thickness in MCI: the right superior parietal lobule and the left posterior insula. A significant Group × Sadness interaction indicated that the association between left superior parietal gray matter volume and sadness recognition differed between groups. Follow-up analyses of the extracted values showed a positive association in MCI, although this within-group association did not reach statistical significance, and a significant inverse association in HCs. These findings suggest that early MCI involves selective thinning in association cortices supporting attention and salience processing. The sadness-specific interaction indicates that patients with MCI may rely on preserved superior parietal structure during sadness recognition, a pattern that is consistent with structural reserve accounts, although this interpretation remains speculative given the cross-sectional design.

papers.title: Reward sensitivity is negatively associated with future self-continuity: the mediation role of functional connectivity between the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex and ventrolateral prefrontal cortex.
papers.authors: Shen H, Chen L, Zhao H, Huang J, Yang C, Xiong Z, Zhang Z, Ren Y, Liu Y, Feng T, Feng P.
papers.abstract: Reward Sensitivity refers to individual differences in the perception, evaluation, and emotional response to potential or acquired rewarding stimuli. Future self-continuity refers to the degree of psychological connection, identification, and consistency that individuals perceive between their present self and future self. Although both constructs are known to critically influence intertemporal decision-making and self-control, the shared neurobiological mechanisms linking them remain largely unexplored. To address this question, we used voxel-based morphometry and resting-state functional connectivity analyses to investigate the neural basis underlying the association between reward sensitivity and future self-continuity. Behavioral results showed reward sensitivity exhibited a significant negative correlation with future self-continuity. Moreover, voxel-based morphometry (VBM) revealed that reward sensitivity was negatively associated with gray matter volume in the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex (dmPFC). Furthermore, resting-state functional connectivity (RSFC) analysis demonstrated that the functional connectivity between the dmPFC and the ventrolateral prefrontal cortex (vlPFC) was positively correlated with reward sensitivity. Ultimately, mediation analysis revealed a positive indirect effect, indicating that this dmPFC-vlPFC connectivity acted as a protective neural factor in the negative relationship between reward sensitivity and future self-continuity. In conclusion, the current research offered novel insights into the impact of reward sensitivity on future self-continuity, advancing our understanding of this behavioral connection from a neurobiological perspective.

papers.title: Frequency-dependent, asymmetric, and dynamic alterations of white matter function in primary hemifacial spasm: a multiband resting-state fMRI study.
papers.authors: Ye H, Wang L, Yan J, Pan L, Zhang Y, Fang L, Chen F, Wang D, Ge X.
papers.abstract: Primary hemifacial spasm involves central network reorganization, but white matter functional alterations remain unclear. We acquired resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data from 89 left-sided patients, 92 right-sided patients, and 124 healthy controls. Patients exhibited widespread abnormalities in tracts including the corpus callosum, superior longitudinal fasciculus, and corona radiata. Notably, this remodeling was highly asymmetric: left-sided patients primarily showed increased local neural activity in prefrontal pathways, whereas right-sided patients exhibited increased global network centrality across interhemispheric tracts. Furthermore, these alterations displayed distinct frequency preferences, and certain functional instabilities were exclusively captured by dynamic metrics rather than static analyses. These findings demonstrate that the disorder is associated with time-varying, frequency-specific, and asymmetric white matter functional reorganization, highlighting the value of dynamic and multi-frequency approaches in decoding its pathophysiology.

papers.title: Brain imaging in dystrophinopathies.
papers.authors: Lancien M, Leboucq N, Desguerre I, Rivier F, Vaillend C.
papers.abstract: Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophies (DMD, BMD) are caused by genetic variants in the DMD gene coding dystrophin proteins. In addition to the impairment of muscular function, these patients also present frequent cognitive and neuropsychiatric disorders due to impaired expression of several brain dystrophins: Dp427, Dp140 and Dp71. Cerebral imaging has shed new light on the impact of dystrophinopathies on brain structure, function, and connectivity. We review the brain imaging results obtained in patients and divers animal models, showing presence of mild cortical atrophy, slight modifications of structures volumes, decreased cerebral blood flood, white matter microstructure alterations, brain hypometabolism, altered connectivity, and an abnormal cerebral response to stress. We further discuss the putative progression of cerebral disorders, and their variable severity when Dp140 expression is affected in addition to that of Dp427. Some correlations between imaging parameters and cognitive and psychological impairments have been reported but remain to be confirmed.

papers.title: The Importance of Translational Research for Neurodevelopmental Disorders and Autism Spectrum Disorders.
papers.authors: Silverman JL, Haouchine OY, Roy D, Monsen ER.
papers.abstract: Translational research is the process of transforming fundamental biological discoveries into safe and efficacious interventions for patients. This specialized field is of particular importance for neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), a broad class of behaviorally defined conditions including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDDs), and related disorders. NDDs present unique translational challenges including (i) a lack of biological diagnostic markers; (ii) the fact that they are diagnosed exclusively by behavioral criteria; (iii) their involvement of dysfunction in complex brain circuitry; and (iv) that there is no single unifying biological mechanism. This chapter reviews the current landscape of translational neuroscience for NDDs, examining the strengths and limitations of preclinical model systems, including rodent models humanized mice, human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) 3D spheroids and brain organoids. This work emphasizes that research emanating from the varying preclinical experimental systems above should be leveraged and their complementary strengths integrated, coordinated, and considered collaboratively, to strengthen current knowledge, identify the remaining research gaps, and prioritize future research. We also emphasize the importance of rigorous, reproducible methodology and conservative interpretation of behavioral and functional outcomes. Discussion is presented on key translational bridges or connections that are urgently required to advance the field: bridging non-human model systems to humanized models, identifying and validating translational biomarkers, bridging in vitro and in vivo findings, and developing corroborative alternatives to animal models. It is our stance that integrating multiple complementary model systems, limiting erroneous behavioral inferences, relying on evolutionarily conserved circuits, and prioritizing robust and reproducible outcome measures will reduce failures in the translational pipeline and accelerate the development of meaningful therapies for individuals with NDDs.

papers.title: Accelerated Motion-Compensated Diffusion-Weighted pCASL Using Subspace Low-Rank Reconstruction for Quantification of BBB Water Exchange and Permeability.
papers.authors: Liu Z, Zhao C, Huang Z, Guo F, Wang DJJ, Shao X.
papers.abstract: Purpose To develop an accelerated motion-compensated diffusion-weighted pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (MCDW-pCASL) method using a spatial subspace low-rank reconstruction method for efficient quantification of blood-brain barrier (BBB) water exchange (kw ) and permeability (PSw). Methods An accelerated multidelay MCDW-pCASL sequence was developed to simultaneously encode intravascular and extravascular diffusion-weighted ASL signals across multiple post-labeling delays (PLDs). A spatial subspace low-rank reconstruction framework was optimized to enable joint estimation of cerebral blood flow (CBF) and BBB water exchange rate and permeability. Fourteen young healthy adults underwent test-retest scans (separated by ∼1 week) at 3 T with both the accelerated MCDW-pCASL (acceleration factor = 3) and a conventional diffusion-prepared (DP) pCASL sequence. Whole-brain, gray-matter, and white-matter CBF and kw values were quantified to assess test-retest repeatability and cross-method agreement. An additional cohort of 30 older adults underwent single-session MCDW and DP scans to evaluate age-related perfusion and BBB kw /PSw differences. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) were used to assess reliability and agreement. Results Accelerated MCDW-pCASL demonstrated excellent agreement with DP-pCASL for CBF (ICC = 0.89) and fair agreement for kw (ICC = 0.56). Test-retest repeatability of MCDW-pCASL was good for CBF, BBB, kw , and PSw (ICC ≈ 0.6). Across both sequences, younger subjects exhibited significantly higher CBF and kw compared with older adults. Conclusion Incorporating a spatial low-rank subspace reconstruction enables accelerated MCDW-pCASL acquisition with reliable simultaneous quantification of CBF, BBB kw , and PSw. Clinical applications of this method for assessing perfusion and BBB function are warranted.

papers.title: Intratumoral and Peritumoral Functional Connectivity Reveals Network-Level Signatures of Glioma.
papers.authors: Bao H, Bai Y, Hu J, Ding W, Lai J, Zalesky A, Tian YE, Tie Y, Mei J, Fang S, Fan X, Luna LP, Jones CK, Ren J, Cui W, Yan J, Yan Z, Wang Z, Zhang R, Lv Z, Jiao Y, Jiang T, Liang P, Sair HI, Wang Y.
papers.abstract: Gliomas are recognized as network-level diseases that remodel functional connectivity across the brain. Using resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) data from 306 patients with pathologically confirmed glioma at two hospitals, we delineated individualized intra- and peritumoral functional networks to quantify tumor-related alterations. Two novel indices-the ratio of intratumoral functional regions (RIFR) and ratio of peritumoral tumor-related regions (RPTR)-were proposed to describe network remodeling. Both indices were related to pathological, structural, functional, cognitive, language, and survival measures. Lower RIFR indicated diminished intratumoral connectivity and worse prognosis, while higher values reflected preserved network integration and longer survival. Models incorporating network features yielded areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.90 in training and 0.86-0.88 in external validation. Supporting analyses suggested that intratumoral functional regions are associated with distinct molecular and cellular characteristics. These findings suggest that intra- and peritumoral networks reflect biologically and functionally distinct tumor subregions and are associated with network-level alterations, brain function, and patient outcome. Interpretation is limited by the hemodynamic basis of rs-fMRI, incomplete data, and limited intraoperative validation. These findings identify individualized intra- and peritumoral connectivity measures as candidate markers of glioma-associated network remodeling and prognosis that require prospective, multimodal validation.

papers.title: Multimodal modeling of the ictal onset zone in refractory insular epilepsy and seizure outcome of magnetic resonance-guided laser interstitial therapy: A pediatric single-center retrospective study.
papers.authors: Guida L, Losito E, Rodrigo S, Chiron C, Fillon L, Bourgeois M, Kaminska A, Pallud J, Chemaly N, Dangouloff-Ross V, Aunvin S, Dozieres B, Nabbout R, David O, Boddaert N, Blauwblomme T.
papers.abstract: Objective This study was undertaken to evaluate seizure outcomes after magnetic resonance-guided laser interstitial thermal therapy (MRgLITT) in children with insular epilepsy and to assess how the extent of ablation overlaps with multimodal definitions of the ictal onset zone (IOZ). Methods We conducted a retrospective, single-center study including consecutive pediatric patients treated with MRgLITT for insular epilepsy. All patients underwent presurgical evaluation including electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI); fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) and stereo-EEG (SEEG) were performed in negative-MRI cases. Epileptic zone was identified by visual analysis of SEEG recording. Postablation contrast-enhancing volumes were manually segmented and coregistered with IOZ estimates derived from Multi-centre Epilepsy Lesion Detection (MELD) MRI analysis, FDG-PET voxel-based analysis, and the Epileptogenicity Index, when available. Spatial concordance between modalities was assessed using Dice similarity coefficients, and the proportion of each IOZ modality encompassed within the ablation volume was correlated with postoperative seizure outcomes (International League Against Epilepsy classification). Results Eight children (median age = 10.4 years, range = 2.3-17) were included, with a median postoperative follow-up of 38 months. Two patients had insular tumors, and both achieved seizure freedom after complete ablation. Among the six MRI-negative patients, FDG-PET revealed insular hypometabolism in four, MELD detected a median of one insular cluster (range 1-3), and SEEG identified focal insular ictal activity in three cases. Overall, four negative-MRI patients achieved seizure freedom: three after MRgLITT alone and one after MRgLITT combined with frontal opercular resection. One transient postoperative aphasia was observed. Intermodality spatial concordance was low across all comparisons. A greater proportion of FDG-PET hypometabolism included in the ablation volume was associated with better seizure outcomes (p = .012). Significance MRgLITT is an effective and safe treatment option for focal insular epilepsy in children, either as standalone therapy or in a combined approach. Optimal outcome depends on accurate preoperative delineation of the IOZ and its complete ablation.

papers.title: Supramodal Coding of Detection and Confidence in the Human Cortex
papers.authors: Porte P, Robin A, Boscher F, Dezier C, Goueytes D, Mahdian S, Hoffmann D, Kahane P, Minotti L, Pereira M, Caron-Guyon J, Goupil L, Faivre N.
papers.abstract: Perception is inherently multisensory, yet it remains unclear whether the brain detects stimuli and evaluates confidence in these detections using circuits shared across senses or circuits specific to each modality. Prior evidence is limited: scalp electrophysiology cannot localize where a shared code operates, whereas functional imaging cannot resolve its timing. We recorded intracranial activity (stereoelectroencephalography) in eight patients with epilepsy who performed a near-threshold audiovisual detection task in which they reported, on each trial, whether a visual, auditory, or audiovisual stimulus was present and rated their confidence, both overall and separately for each modality. Analyzing high-gamma activity at the single-channel and region-of-interest levels, we found that stimulus detection involved a broadly distributed, largely supramodal set of cortical regions responding regardless of modality, including the insula, dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, and superior temporal gyrus. Multivariate decoders trained to distinguish detected from undetected stimuli in one modality generalized to the other modality, indicating a shared detection code within these regions. Confidence relied on a more mixed architecture but was also substantially supramodal. Finally, the auditory cortex encoded confidence information about its non-preferred (visual) modality, with a similar effect in the visual cortex for auditory confidence, suggesting that the involvement of sensory cortices in confidence is not confined to its preferred input.

papers.title: Real-time noise cancellation for EEG monitoring and brain–computer interfaces
papers.authors: Makkonen M, Kahilakoski O, Metsomaa J, Lioumis P, Ilmoniemi RJ, Mutanen TP.
papers.abstract: A bstract Raw electroencephalography (EEG) data suffer from a low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Effective real-time cleaning of EEG would improve the robustness of EEG monitoring, brain–computer interfaces, and brain-state-dependent stimulation applications in both laboratory and real-life environments. Here, we present a real-time source-estimate-utilizing noise-discarding algorithm (rtSOUND) for EEG noise suppression. We adapted the established offline SOUND algorithm for real-time use and implemented it into an open-source EEG-processing software. Instead of using conventional temporal filtering, SOUND operates the data with a spatial filter. This makes it particularly suitable for real-time applications, since each streamed data sample can be cleaned separately in near real-time. Unlike temporal filtering methods, SOUND does not make assumptions about the frequency content of noise and brain signals but assumes that the noise topographies differ from those generated by brain activity. With an EEG forward model, rtSOUND cross-validates the EEG time series and estimates the spatial distribution of noise, resulting in a data-cleaning linear spatial filter. Each streamed EEG sample is processed synchronously, and the filter is periodically updated in an asynchronous parallel process. The algorithm rapidly updates the spatial filter in response to changes in the data, ensuring that noise reduction is both immediate and accurately adapted to the current EEG state. rtSOUND was validated with transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS)–EEG and resting-state EEG datasets measured from 25 healthy subjects. SNR of both TMS-evoked potentials and resting-state data consistently improved across various metrics. rtSOUND particularly benefitted channels with poor SNR, while retaining the waveforms in high-quality channels. The algorithm was fast enough to process data streamed at 5 kHz. rtSOUND improves the SNR of EEG in real time, providing a robust method to improve signal quality for brain-state-monitoring applications.

papers.title: Understanding Performance Plateaus and Representation Collapse in 3D MRI Transformers Trained to Classify Brain Disease
papers.authors: Chattopadhyay T, Shelar K, Thomopoulos SI, Thompson PM.
papers.abstract: A bstract In medical imaging AI, we commonly assume that diagnostic classifiers will increase in accuracy if they are trained on more data, but in reality, their performance often plateaus. To understand this behavior, we ran a spectral analysis of 3D vision transformers, a common supervised deep learning model that can be trained to classify disease based on 3D brain MRI. For simpler classification methods such as linear discriminant analysis, the classifier performance AUC(N), when trained on a sample of size N, is known to depend on the encoder’s eigenspectrum. Each class-discriminative direction in the latent space contributes only after the sample size N reaches a threshold N i = λ i /α i 2 - so the spectrum influences how performance scales with training data. Building on this theory, we show that supervised transformers compress almost all of their discriminative signal into one principal component (EVR@1 = 0.90–0.96): after this “representation collapse” happens, no further directions cross the threshold as training data increases, and accuracy plateaus. In principle, this plateau in performance could be due to either the encoder’s learned feature space or the difficulty of the task. To distinguish these cases, we trained three types of supervised 3D transformers (ViT3D, MINiT, NIT) and, as a non-collapsing alternative, a frozen self-supervised encoder (DINO), to classify people with dementia or mild cognitive impairment (MCI) versus cognitively normal (CN) individuals from 3D brain MRI, using data from the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). We froze each encoder and applied it to a new task, so that only the task difficulty varied. An “easy” task encoder (Dementia vs CN), transferred to the harder task (MCI vs CN), did not reproduce the plateau (MINiT threshold 9.2), but full retraining did (2758.5). The plateau is therefore due to the learned encoder, rather than task difficulty. Ranking the feature directions by the proportion of the disease signal they contain, we were able to identify a sign of representation collapse, i.e., a single dominant spike in the latent feature eigenspectrum. This spike was 11–26 times larger than predicted from the rest of the spectrum for the disease-trained (supervised) encoders, but was absent for DINO (0.66). To predict how transformer accuracy scales with the number of training scans, a large spike in the encoder spectrum suggests that the representation has collapsed and additional scans will not help; a small spike means that the signal is spread across many encoder latent space directions, and more training data should boost the classifier performance.

papers.title: Structural topology shapes regional roles in neuronal avalanche initiation and termination
papers.authors: De Luca M, Demuru M, Troisi Lopez E, Gallo E, Cafaro G, Duma GM, Depannemaecker D, Casagrande G, Quarantelli M, Granata C, Sorrentino G, Sorrentino P, Angiolelli M.
papers.abstract: Whole-brain dynamics unfold as fast, discrete, transient events known as neuronal avalanches, whose propagation is constrained by the connectome, that is, the large-scale scaffolding of structural connections wiring the brain. However, the role of the connectome in determining the topographies of the start and end of these transient cascades remains unclear. Leveraging resting-state Magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings and diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) tractography across 42 healthy individuals, we examined whether the structural architecture of white matter tracts dictates the spatial origins and the end of cortical avalanches. We found that the probability of triggering and finishing an avalanche is strongly related to the structural nodal strength, showing a positive correlation that is highly robust to non-parametric spatial permutation testing and bootstrapping. This structure-function coupling is highly stable and robust across different activation thresholds, demonstrating that the choice of avalanche extraction threshold does not drive or alter our main findings. Collectively, our results suggest that structural properties determine a region’s propensity to initiate and terminate neuronal avalanches.

papers.title: T-cell dysregulation is implicated in the encephalopathy of prematurity
papers.authors: Smikle-Bernard R, Blesa Cábez M, Vaher K, Amir R, Mckinnon K, Murphy L, Thrippleton MJ, Quigley AJ, Bastin ME, Reynolds RM, Whalley HC, Marioni RE, Cox SR, Boardman JP.
papers.abstract: Preterm birth is strongly linked to systemic inflammation and encephalopathy of prematurity, which underlies subsequent cognitive impairment. T-cell immunity contributes to brain-immune crosstalk across the life course but its role in the pathogenesis of encephalopathy of prematurity is unknown. Protein epigenetic scores are DNA methylation (DNAm)-based proxies of circulating proteins. We tested the hypothesis that T-cell dysregulation has a specific role in child neurodevelopment following preterm birth. Multimodal data were collected from 144 preterm infants (median gestational age at birth 29 + 5 weeks [range 23 + 3 to 32 + 6 ]) recruited to a prospective cohort study: saliva DNAm for protein epigenetic score derivation and brain MRI, both at term-equivalent age, and the Mullen Scales of Early Learning Composite score at 5 years from a subset. We investigated associations of the epigenetic scores for cytotoxic and regulatory T cell-associated molecule (DNAm CRTAM) and C-reactive protein (DNAm CRP; a non-specific marker of inflammation) with MRI metrics of encephalopathy of prematurity: global and regional brain volumes, and general factors of diffusion tensor imaging and neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging metrics averaged across 42 white matter tracts. We tested whether DNAm CRTAM explains more variance than DNAm CRP in MRI metrics of the encephalopathy of prematurity and cognitive scores in childhood. Higher neonatal DNAm CRTAM was associated with lower general factor of fractional anisotropy (β = −0.252, q = 0.011) and higher general factors of radial diffusivity (β = 0.215, q = 0.039), mean diffusivity (β = 0.198, q = 0.047) and orientation dispersion index (β = 0.201, q = 0.048), independent of inflammatory morbidities and other biological covariates after false discovery rate correction. DNAm CRTAM explained more variance than DNAm CRP (maximum incremental R 2 = 4.2% vs 1.5%) in diffusion MRI metrics. Higher neonatal DNAm CRTAM was associated with lower cognitive scores at 5 years, independent of DNAm CRP and other covariates (β = −0.332, P = 0.008), and explained more variance in cognitive scores than DNAm CRP (incremental R 2 = 9.4% vs 1.2%). An epigenetic proxy of CRTAM in preterm infants is associated with both encephalopathy of prematurity in the neonatal period and lower cognitive performance at 5 years, explaining greater incremental variance than a non-specific marker of inflammation. The data implicate T-cell dysregulation in the pathophysiology of atypical neurodevelopment following preterm birth.

papers.title: Sex- and age-dependent control of dopamine function by LRRK2, and rapid reversal of dopamine release deficits in the LRRK2-G2019S knock-in mouse model of Parkinson’s Disease
papers.authors: Gentle C, Kamesh A, Madranges J, Coady S, Viera B, Tifensee-Ribiero C, McClean S, Kuhlmann N, Khayachi A, Pietrantonio A, Moulanier L, Cohen E, Farrer M, Parsons M, Milnerwood A.
papers.abstract: No disease-modifying therapy exists for Parkinson’s disease (PD). At diagnosis (∼65y), ∼70% of nigrostriatal dopamine (DA) axons may have degenerated, so identifying when and how striatal axon function declines is critical. LRRK2 hyperactivity is observed in LRRK2 and VPS35 familial cases, and also idiopathic PD. Thus suggests LRRK2 hyperfunction is a common pathophysiological feature of PD. LRRK2 inhibitors are currently in human trials, yet their effects on brain circuit function are poorly characterized. By optical imaging of iGluSnFR and dLight we measured striatal glutamate and DA release in WT, LRRK2 G2019S (LKI) and VPS35 D620N (VKI) knock-in mice, across adult ages and sexes, with and without LRRK2 inhibition. In WT mice, ongoing LRRK2 activity regulated DA release in an age- and sex-dependent manner. Acute inhibition reversed basal sex differences in striatal glutamate and DA release in aged mice, and potentiated DA release more in middle-aged females than males.
