By using multimodal neuroimaging, the present study aims to investigate the immediate neural substrates underlying acupuncture stimulation in patients with ASD. These findings are expected to provide a robust neurobiological foundation for future longitudinal research and the development of evidence-based integrative strategies.

papers.title: Cerebral Attack With Cortical-Leptomeningeal Involvement and Seizures in AQP4-IgG-Positive Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder.
papers.authors: Miyamoto M, Sato Y, Ishii N.
papers.abstract: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) rarely presents with corticalleptomeningeal involvement. A 47-year-old woman with aquaporin-4 immunoglobulin G (AQP4-IgG)-positive NMOSD developed acute headache, seizures, motor aphasia, and worsening right arm weakness. Brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed a tumefactive-appearing left frontal cortical-subcortical lesion with leptomeningeal enhancement. The clinical and radiological abnormalities improved after immunotherapy. This case illustrates a rare cerebral manifestation of AQP4-IgG-positive NMOSD with cortical-leptomeningeal involvement, seizures, and a tumefactive lesion.

papers.title: Effective Connectivity and Clinical Correlates in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
papers.authors: Han KI, Bae JH, Jo HJ, Park JM, Yeo Y, Park TS, Park DW, Kim TH.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.abstract: Background Cognitive impairment is a substantial comorbidity in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, the neural mechanisms underlying this association remain poorly understood. This study aimed to assess alterations in effective connectivity (EC) in patients with COPD and investigate their relationships with clinical measures. Methods Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (RS-fMRI) was performed in 38 patients with COPD and 30 healthy controls. EC was estimated using vector autoregressive (VAR) modelling combined with Granger causality analysis across 26 prespecified brain regions of interest derived from our previous functional connectivity study of the same cohort. Between-group differences in directed connectivity were assessed using Welch's t -tests. Associations between EC measures showing between-group differences and clinical measures were evaluated using age-adjusted partial Pearson correlations. Results At the nominal two-sided p < 0.05 level, 37 directed connections showed between-group differences in effective connectivity, and the mean vector autoregressive coefficients for 35 of these connections lay on opposite sides of zero between the COPD and control groups. Among the connections showing between-group differences, age-adjusted associations in patients with COPD involved pulmonary function, systemic oxygenation, cognition, affect, and health status. These associations involved distributed cortical, subcortical, and cerebellar regions, with several directed connections showing convergence across multiple clinical domains. Conclusion Resting-state VAR-based EC revealed distributed between-group differences in direction-sensitive BOLD temporal organization in COPD. Several of these EC measures were associated with pulmonary function, SpO2 , respiratory and COPD symptom burden, cognition, affect, and health status after age adjustment. These findings extend the functional connectivity profile of COPD by linking directed temporal relationships to its multidimensional clinical burden.

papers.title: EEG microstate-source coupling is spatially preserved in ALS
papers.authors: Metzger M, Costa G, Dukic S, McMackin R, Giglia E, Mitchell M, Bista S, Tadjine Y, Sirenko V, Plaitano S, Coffey A, Sharp AF, Mehra P, Suleyman N, Woods E, Heverin M, Bede P, Muthuraman M, Pender N, Hardiman O, Nasseroleslami B.
papers.abstract: Abstract EEG microstates are thought to reflect rapid transitions between brain-wide states and show disrupted temporal dynamics across neurological and psychiatric conditions, including ALS, yet the neural sources generating these states remain incompletely understood. Here, we introduce a source-resolved framework that links time-resolved microstate activations to estimated regional brain signals, enabling estimation of the neural sources underlying canonical microstate classes. Resting-state EEG from a large cohort of healthy controls (HC, n = 122) and individuals with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS, n = 121) was analysed. Canonical microstates were derived from pooled data, and time-resolved microstate activation time series were estimated via projection-based decomposition of scalp potentials. In parallel, EEG source activity was reconstructed using beamformer-based inverse modelling and parcellated into 90 cortical regions. Microstate-source coupling was quantified using ridge regression linking microstate activations to reconstructed regional timecourses, producing spatially resolved coupling maps for each microstate class. In HC, reproducible and spatially distinct microstate-source coupling patterns were observed, consistent with structured mapping between scalp-defined brain states and distributed neural systems. Spatial reproducibility was confirmed using permutation-based null models that preserved temporal autocorrelation within microstate sequences and accounted for spatial dependence across regions. In HC, microstate-source coupling was spatially reproducible across independent subgroups for the four canonical microstates (A-D; r ≥ 0.90, q < 0.05). In ALS, coupling topography was preserved relative to HC for all four microstate classes (r ≥ 0.90, q < 0.05), and cluster-based permutation testing revealed no significant group differences in coupling magnitude for any microstate class, a null result robust to sex and riluzole status. Microstate-source coupling was preserved, suggesting stability of canonical microstate organisation across sensor and source space. Overall, these findings demonstrate that canonical EEG microstates have stable, reproducible coupling with distributed brain sources, and that this coupling organisation is preserved in ALS despite known alterations in microstate temporal characteristics. This dissociation suggests that spatial and temporal organisation of microstates may be governed by partially independent mechanisms, with spatial organisation buffered against ALS-related change, potentially through degeneracy or local compensatory mechanisms, while temporal engagement remains more directly sensitive to disease.

papers.title: Neuro-JEPA: Building and Evaluating Health-System Scale Neuroimaging Foundation Models with Mixture of Experts
papers.authors: Huang H, Chen L, Chen J, Hyun J, Loftus J, Melmed K, Orringer D, Frontera J, Dehkharghani S, Masurkar A, Razavian N.
papers.abstract: Abstract Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain routinely combines complementary contrasts—including T1-weighted (T1w), T2-weighted (T2w) and FLAIR sequences—to capture anatomy and pathology. Although foundation models trained on large neuroimaging datasets have shown promise, it remains unclear whether they effectively integrate these complementary contrasts across diverse clinical settings. Here we present Neuro-JEPA, a multimodal foundation model that learns unified representations across structural brain MRIs. Neuro-JEPA combines latent predictive learning with a sparse Mixture-of-Experts architecture to encode multiple MRI contrasts within a single model. The model is pretrained on 1.55 million scans from 428,647 clinical imaging studies spanning T1w, T2w and FLAIR sequences. The model performance is evaluated on 47 downstream tasks across three independent health systems and 12 public datasets, encompassing single-contrast, multimodal and cross-domain applications. Across these evaluations, Neuro-JEPA achieved the strongest overall performance and generalized robustly across heterogeneous cohorts, outperforming existing neuroimaging foundation models and strong conventional baselines in the majority of comparisons despite using less than one-third of the pretraining data of leading models. Performance gains were particularly pronounced in data-scarce settings, reaching up to 15% over prior foundation models for clinically important pathologies including gliosis and multiple sclerosis. Neuro-JEPA showed clinically relevant capabilities across domains, including prediction of amyloid status and progression from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer’s disease dementia, stroke identification and classification, and prediction of post-stroke functional outcome and length of stay. Together, these results show that data scale, curation and principled model design can act synergistically to produce broadly transferable neuroimaging representations, and establish Neuro-JEPA as a scalable framework toward general-purpose multimodal foundation models for neurological imaging.

papers.title: A Restricted No-Go Theorem for Exact, Coherent, and Isolated Quantum Learning Architectures
papers.authors: Majumdar MG.
papers.abstract: Abstract The straightforward translation of classical machine learning models into the quantum domain is obstructed by fundamental structural constraints of quantum mechanics. In this work, we rigorously examine the interplay between universality, coherent training, and isolation in quantum learning systems. We prove a restricted no-go theorem: within the setting of exact continuous unitary hypothesis classes, finite-dimensional closed quantum systems, and fully coherent parameter-update rules with no intermediate measurement or classical feedback, no architecture can simultaneously satisfy universality (U), coherent training (C), and isolation (I). This result follows from a synthesis of the no-programming theorem, linearity of quantum dynamics, and the necessity of measurement for performance evaluation. Crucially, we distinguish between (i) nonlinear functions applied to classical parameter values encoded in a computational basis, which are permitted, and (ii) deterministic nonlinear transformations on arbitrary unknown quantum states, which are forbidden. Our analysis shows that many naively quantized models, such as fully coherent versions of neural networks, support vector machines, and principal component analysis, either incur substantial state-preparation overheads or violate the structural rules of quantum theory. We conclude that viable quantum machine learning (QML) architectures must relax the isolation condition, thereby justifying the dominant hybrid classical-quantum paradigm not as a mere engineering compromise, but as a physical necessity imposed by the UCI constraints.

papers.title: The Microbiome–Sleep–Psychiatric Axis: Does Circadian Disruption Mediate Microbiome-Associated Psychiatric Risk?
papers.authors: S. V SK.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome is studied as a modulator of brain function and a contributor to psychiatric pathophysiology, while sleep and circadian disruption are transdiagnostic psychiatric risk factors. Because the gut microbiota oscillates with host circadian clocks, a three-way “microbiome–sleep–psychiatric axis” has been proposed in which circadian disruption mediates microbiome-associated psychiatric risk. This narrative review translates that axis into an explicit counterfactual mediation framework with named paths, stated identification assumptions, and testable predictions, and appraises the evidence against it. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science to 30 June 2026, report the strategy in full, and tabulate 18 key human studies and each candidate pathway. The mediator–outcome path is well supported in humans, including by Mendelian randomization, but effect sizes are modest (insomnia–depression pooled OR ≈ 2.1–2.8). The exposure–mediator path is demonstrated only in rodents under extreme perturbation, and microbiome–psychiatry associations are small (β-diversity explaining roughly 0.5–2% of variance). Candidate pathways – glucocorticoid rhythmicity, tryptophan–kynurenine metabolism, short-chain fatty acid signalling, vagal transmission, and microglial–neuroimmune crosstalk – each support one limb of the chain and none the whole. Critically, no human study has estimated any mediated effect, and no cohort has measured the microbiome, a validated circadian phenotype, and psychiatric outcomes with temporal ordering. Existing data remain equally compatible with reverse causation and with confounding by shared environmental disruptors. The circadian mediation hypothesis is therefore falsifiable but untested; we specify the cohort, Mendelian randomization, natural-experiment, and interventional designs that would confirm or refute it.

papers.title: Integrated Serum Pharmacochemistry and Investigation of the 2 Anti-Depression Effect of Chaihu–Huangqin Drug Pair
papers.authors: Wang S, Yang T, Liu T, Zhang Z, Huang C, Liao M, Cai Y, Chen Y.
papers.abstract: Background: Chaihu–Huangqin (CHHQ, Bupleuri Radix–Scutellariae Radix) is the core drug pair of Xiaochaihu Decoction, yet the constituents that reach the brain and the pathways they engage remain largely unknown. Methods: An integrated strategy combining serum pharmacochemistry, brain-region-resolved distribution profiling, network pharmacology, molecular docking, and in vivo validation was developed in a chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) rat model. Results: UPLC-MS/MS-based serum pharmacochemistry identified 97 constituents absorbed into the systemic circulation. In CUMS rats, CHHQ ameliorated depressive-like behaviors, evidenced by increased sucrose preference and reduced immobility in the forced swimming test, without evident hepatic or renal toxicity. Profiling across six depression-related brain regions revealed the largest number of region-specific candidates in the dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN), which was therefore selected as the focus region. Network pharmacology prioritized inflammatory and serotonergic signaling, including the nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB)/NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3)/Caspase-1 axis and the serotonin transporter (SERT), and molecular docking gave GlideScore values of −6.01 to −10.50. In the DRN, CHHQ attenuated microglial activation, decreased TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-18, and downregulated NF-κB, NLRP3, and Caspase-1, accompanied by restored SERT expression. Conclusion: These findings establish an “absorption into blood—brain-region-resolved detection—DRN candidate prioritization” workflow and provide new insights into the material basis and multi-target mechanism of the CHHQ drug pair.

papers.title: The hypothalamic orexin-medial prefrontal cortex pathway modulates susceptibility to depression in the learned helplessness paradigm in male mice.
papers.authors: Mi T, He Z, Yu B, Li Q, Lu G, Hao J, Niu J, Ma S, Rong W, Niu J.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.abstract: Depression is a prevalent psychiatric disorder primarily characterized by behavioral despair and helplessness. The orexinergic system plays a crucial role in stress-induced depression; however, the precise mechanisms remain unclear. The medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), a major target of orexinergic projections, is essential for emotional regulation. This study suggests that impaired orexinergic input to the mPFC underlies depression-like behaviors in murine models. In the learned helplessness (LH) paradigm, the majority of male mice subjected to inescapable foot shocks developed depression-like behaviors (classified as LH-susceptible), whereas a subset displayed resilience (classified as LH-resilient). LH-susceptible mice exhibited a reduced number of orexin+ neuronal somata in the hypothalamus, along with decreased expression of prepro-orexin mRNA Correspondingly, the mPFC of these mice displayed decreased density of orexinergic terminals and lower Orexin A levels. In contrast, LH-resilient mice maintained stable hypothalamic orexin neuron counts, exhibited increased prepro-orexin mRNA expression, and preserved orexinergic terminal density in the mPFC. Chemogenetic activation of the hypothalamic orexin-mPFC pathway alleviated depression-like behaviors in LH-susceptible mice through Orexin A signaling. Conversely, inhibition of this pathway induced depression-like behaviors in LH-resilient mice. Additionally, LH-susceptible mice showed decreased excitatory synaptic transmission in layer V pyramidal neurons of the mPFC, which was improved by activation of hypothalamic orexinergic inputs; this improvement was attenuated by administration of an orexin receptor 1 (OX1R) antagonist. Collectively, these findings implicate the hypothalamic orexin-mPFC pathway as a pivotal regulator of excitatory synaptic transmission and suggest its involvement in modulating individual variability in susceptibility and resilience to depression.Significance statement Depression is a highly prevalent emotional disorder characterized by behavioral despair and helplessness under stress. This study demonstrates that the orexinergic system is critical for modulating resilience to aversive stimuli. Using the learned helplessness (LH) mouse model, we found that LH-susceptible mice, but not LH-resilient mice, show compromised hypothalamic orexinergic projections to the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), together with decreased excitatory synaptic transmission in layer V pyramidal neurons. Activation of the hypothalamic orexin-mPFC pathway alleviates depression-like behaviors in susceptible mice through Orexin A, while inhibition of this pathway induces depression-like phenotypes in resilient mice. These findings identify orexinergic signaling as a promising therapeutic target for depression.

papers.title: Scalp EEG and Intrinsic Optical Signal Imaging for Noninvasive Detection of Spreading Depolarizations in the Rat Cortex.
papers.authors: Mingazov B, Tukhvatullina K, Khazipov R, Nasretdinov A.
papers.abstract: Spreading depolarization (SD) is a slowly propagating wave of massive neuronal and glial depolarization in the cerebral cortex that occurs in various brain diseases. However, noninvasive SD detection remains challenging. Here, we used scalp EEG and intrinsic optical signal (IOS) recordings in rats of both sexes to assess the feasibility of noninvasively detecting high-potassium-induced SDs in the cortex. Scalp EEG failed to detect DC-shifts but revealed a characteristic SD-related depression of AC-EEG activity, while concurrent infrared IOS recordings captured reliable SD-associated signals. Although the magnitudes of AC-EEG depression and IOS signals during scalp recordings were several times smaller than those recorded epidurally, both techniques enabled high-fidelity SD detection. These findings demonstrate that noninvasive monitoring of scalp EEG and infrared IOS imaging reliably detects SDs in the rat cerebral cortex.

papers.title: Asymmetric Synaptic Plasticity Provides an Attractor-Based Mechanism for θ-γ Coupling and Pathological Synchronization.
papers.authors: Bi H, Wang B, Deng H, Tian C, Zhang X.
papers.abstract: Short-term synaptic plasticity continuously reshapes the balance between excitation and inhibition, yet most population models assume that excitatory and inhibitory synapses share similar short-term dynamics. Experimental studies, however, have shown that inhibitory synapses typically exhibit stronger short-term depression (STD) than recurrent excitatory connections. Here, we investigate how this cell-type-specific asymmetry influences cortical population dynamics by combining a neural mass model with large-scale spiking network simulations. We show that asymmetric inhibitory STD qualitatively changes the attractor structure of the network, generating a bistable regime that is absent under the conventional symmetric assumption. Within this regime, endogenous finite-size fluctuations drive spontaneous transitions between a stable focus and a stable limit cycle, giving rise to metastable dynamics. The asymmetric paradigm exhibits θ -γ phase-amplitude coupling of strength similar to that of the symmetric one, although it arises from fundamentally different dynamics. We further show that slowing synaptic recovery progressively eliminates this bistable regime, leading to persistent hypersynchronous oscillations and reduced phase-amplitude coupling. These results identify asymmetric inhibitory STD as a mechanism that reshapes cortical attractor dynamics and suggest how altered synaptic recovery may contribute to pathological network activity.

papers.title: Functional and Structural Imaging Features of Cognitive Profiles in Multiple Sclerosis.
papers.authors: Jain K, Valsasina P, Mistri D, Meani A, Preziosa P, Filippi M, Rocca MA.
papers.abstract: Background and objectives Cognitive impairment affects 40%-70% of patients with multiple sclerosis (MS). Although recent hypothesis-driven and data-driven efforts have identified cognitive phenotypes, functional substrates underlying impairment in such phenotypes are still not clear. Our objective was to identify distinct cognitive phenotypes using clustering in a large cohort of patients with MS and characterize their associated clinical, structural MRI, and resting-state (RS) functional connectivity (FC) features. Methods We conducted an observational, cross-sectional study with right-handed patients with MS and age-matched and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs) who underwent neurologic and neuropsychological evaluation (Brief Repeatable Battery of Neuropsychological tests). Latent profile analysis on cognitive test Z-scores identified MS cognitive phenotypes. 3.0T MRI was used to derive atrophy measures and RS FC within default mode network (DMN I/II), executive control network (ECN), left/right fronto-parietal, language, and salience networks. Linear regression models compared structural MRI and RS FC across cognitive phenotypes and HCs, while polynomial contrasts assessed RS FC patterns across groups. Results Three hundred and sixty-nine patients with MS and 168 HCs were enrolled. Four cognitive phenotypes were detected: preserved cognition ([PC], n = 67[18.2%]), mild single-domain verbal fluency involvement (MSD-VF, n = 37[10.0%]), mild single-domain attention involvement (MSD-A, n = 197[53.4%]), and severe multidomain (SMD) involvement (SMD, n = 68[18.4%]). At corrected threshold, PC patients showed decreased deep gray matter (GM) volumes (p < 0.001-0.001) and similar RS FC vs HCs, whereas MSD-VF exhibited no significant atrophy and no differences in RS FC vs HCs. MSD-A displayed lower cortical/deep GM volumes vs HCs (p < 0.001-0.005), whereas SMD had worse clinical and atrophy features (p < 0.001-0.04), as well as decreased DMN II RS FC (p = 0.01-0.04) vs other groups. Polynomial contrast analyses revealed significant quadratic patterns with increased RS FC in MSD-VF vs HC/PC groups, followed by decrease in MSD-A and SMD, within DMN II (p = 0.005), ECN (p = 0.005), and language network (p < 0.001). Discussion PC exhibited intact RS FC, whereas SMD presented widespread structural and DMN RS FC damage. These findings advance our understanding of cognitive heterogeneity in MS by revealing distinct structural and functional neuroimaging profiles across cognitive phenotypes, encouraging future longitudinal and multimodal investigations to improve disease characterization and prognostic stratification.

papers.title: Unraveling the Genotype-Phenotype Landscape of Kleefstra Syndrome Through EHMT1 Variant Analysis.
papers.authors: Kim JM, Cha JH, Kim W, Kim SY, Ko JM, Lim B, Lee S, Chae JH.
papers.abstract: Background and objectives Kleefstra syndrome type 1 (KLEFS1) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by pathogenic variants in EHMT1 , which play a key role in epigenetic regulation. Core features include global developmental delay (GDD), intellectual disability (ID), facial dysmorphism, congenital heart defects (CHDs), and neuropsychiatric manifestations. Methods This retrospective study included patients with KLEFS1 evaluated at Seoul National University Hospital between January 2022 and April 2025. Genetic diagnoses were made using chromosomal microarray or whole-exome or whole-genome sequencing, and clinical data were extracted from medical records. To enhance statistical power, we conducted a joint analysis with established cohorts of at least 30 clinically characterized patients. Results Among the 15 patients with KLEFS1, 14 (93.3%) exhibited GDD or ID, with frequent comorbidities such as CHDs (8/12, 66.7%), orthopaedic manifestations (6/12, 50.0%), epilepsy (6/15, 40.0%), and sleep problems (4/11, 36.4%). Brain MRI revealed abnormalities in 10 of the 12 patients (83.3%), including pituitary anomalies in 2 (16.7%). By combining our data with recently published multicenter international cohorts, we assessed genotype-phenotype correlations by comparing the clinical features of 202 patients with different variant subtypes. Patients with multigene deletions had a significantly higher prevalence of CHDs (53.5% vs 25.8%, p value = 2 × 10-4 ), cortical visual impairment (12.5% vs 1.7%, p value = 0.004), microcephaly (37.1% vs 17.8%, p value = 0.009), corpus callosum abnormalities (17.9% vs 5.9%, p value = 0.02), and hearing impairment (39.7% vs 25.6%, p value = 0.04) than those with single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) or short insertions/deletions (indels), in addition to the previously identified features including epilepsy, constipation, and short stature. We also observed that a recurrent EHMT1 variant (p.Arg948Trp), identified in multiple unrelated patients, was linked to significant phenotypic heterogeneity, including late-onset neurocognitive regression. Discussion Our study showed that patients with multigene deletions are significantly more likely to exhibit multiorgan involvement, including CHDs, cortical visual impairments, microcephaly, corpus callosum abnormalities, and hearing impairments, compared with those with SNVs or indels, emphasizing the importance of genotype-informed management. We report pituitary gland abnormalities in KLEFS1, expanding the phenotypic and neuroimaging spectrum of KLEFS1. The patient showing regression in their 30s necessitates long-term, comprehensive studies to support care.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence EEG biomarkers for schizophrenia diagnosis: Systematic review with PROBAST+AI assessment.
papers.authors: Łoś K, Waszkiewicz N.
papers.journal: European psychiatry : the journal of the Association of European Psychiatrists
papers.abstract: Background The application of artificial intelligence (AI) to resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) data represents a burgeoning frontier in schizophrenia diagnostics. However, the inferential validity of findings is frequently compromised by methodological heterogeneity. This systematic review rigorously evaluates the diagnostic efficacy and methodological robustness of AI-generated EEG biomarkers by implementing the Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool for Artificial Intelligence (PROBAST+AI). Methods Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science identified 43 primary studies encompassing 3,420 patients with schizophrenia or first-episode psychosis and 3,164 healthy controls (total N = 6,584). Methodological quality and validation strategies were assessed using the 34 signaling questions of the PROBAST+AI framework. Results The aggregate mean diagnostic accuracy across the literature was 93.38%, with deep learning architectures demonstrating superior metrics relative to classical machine learning (96.83% vs. 87.68%). Critically, external validation was restricted to 4.7% of the included studies. A pronounced performance discrepancy was observed between subject-wise (88.22%) and segment-wise (98.14%) validation protocols, indicating pervasive data leakage. Overall, 76.7% of the analyzed studies were characterized by a high risk of bias, predominantly stemming from suboptimal data partitioning and inadequate independent verification. Conclusions Contemporary diagnostic accuracies appear to be artifactually elevated due to structural methodological deficiencies and data leakage. Consequently, current evidence does not support the immediate clinical implementation of AI-EEG biomarkers in schizophrenia. To facilitate translational progress, we propose a standardized methodological framework optimizing validation strategies.

papers.title: Longitudinal DNA methylation dynamics distinguish persistent and remitted attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in childhood and adolescence.
papers.authors: Wrigglesworth J, Chirokoff V, Fransquet PD, Craig JM, Silk TJ.
papers.journal: European psychiatry : the journal of the Association of European Psychiatrists
papers.abstract: Background Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder, with symptoms that remit or persist over time. Biological mechanisms underlying symptom change remain poorly understood, though epigenetic processes, like DNA methylation (DNAm), may serve as dynamic biomarkers of clinical outcomes. We examined change in DNAm in children and adolescents with and without ADHD, including differences between remitted and persistent ADHD. Methods We analyzed 219 saliva samples from 94 participants (aged 9.5-14.5 years) attending two to three waves of NICAP (Neuroimaging of the Children's Attention Project). DNAm was profiled using the Infinium MethylationEPIC BeadChip. Linear mixed models adjusted for age, sex, medication, batch, and cell-proportion assessed longitudinal change. Comparisons included (1) individuals with versus without ADHD, (2) persistent or remitted ADHD versus without ADHD, and (3) persistent versus remitted ADHD. False discovery rate correction controlled for multiple testing (FDR-adjusted-p < 0.05). Results Comparison (1) showed null findings after correction for multiple testing. In contrast to those without ADHD (2), the average DNAm was statistically different at 2 sites in persistent ADHD (FDR-adjusted-p < 0.05) and 3 sites in remitted ADHD (FDR-adjusted-p < 0.03), and methylation of 3 additional CpGs differentially changed in persistent ADHD (FDR-adjusted-p < 0.04). Remitted differed from persistent ADHD (3) at 4 CpGs, including cg21443143 (ZFAT ), which showed a decline over time. Gene enrichment links findings to brain structures and function, though these did not survive multiple testing. Conclusions Our study identified several epigenetic differences between remitted and persistent ADHD outcomes from typical development, and from each other. Given the early stage of this research, our findings warrant further prospective epigenome-wide studies into these diagnostic trajectories.

papers.title: SALL1 as a marker for distinguishing microglia from blood-derived myeloid cells in stroke brain scRNA-seq data.
papers.authors: Zhang CY, Lu YM, Zhang H, Li YS, He LY, Gao YY, Xue MZ, Wang ZY, Tang ZB, Feng LL, Wang J, Zhang YX.
papers.abstract: Distinguishing resident microglia from infiltrating myeloid cells in stroke scRNA-seq data remains challenging due to shared myeloid markers; SALL1 shows greater specificity for microglia compared with commonly used markers (e.g. TMEM119, CX3CR1, P2RY12), and combining SALL1 with these commonly used markers improves the ability to distinguish microglia from infiltrating myeloid populations in stroke‑associated scRNA‑seq datasets.

papers.title: Middle Cerebral Artery Occlusion-induced Deficits in Fine Skilled Motor Movement and Its Recovery Following Combined Treatment with Sodium Valproate and CIMT.
papers.authors: P G R, Doreswamy Y, T R L.
papers.abstract: Background Preclinical studies have shown that sodium valproic acid (VPA) has neuroprotective properties following ischaemic injury. However, its compatibility as an adjuvant therapy with physical rehabilitation in ischaemic stroke recovery, with underlying neurophysiological mechanisms, has not been explored yet. Purpose The present study has investigated the advantage of combination therapy over monotherapy in ameliorating ischaemic stroke-induced deficits in skilled fine motor movements with associated changes in local and interhemispheric neural connectivity. Methods Cerebral ischaemic stroke was induced by 60 min of middle cerebral artery occlusion in adult male Sprague-Dawley rats. VPA (300 mg/kg, subcutaneously, twice daily) was administered within 3 h after reperfusion and continued for 7 days, followed by constraint-induced movement therapy (CIMT) for another week (6 h/day). The ischaemic stroke phenotype was assessed based on neurological deficits, gait, forelimb use, rotarod stay time, reach success and infarct volume. Functional recovery, with associated changes in neural activities, was carried out by analysing the local field potential signals from the first reach success during the reach-to-grasp task on day 8 and day 15 post-stroke. Cortical oscillations were analysed at delta (0-4 Hz), theta (4-8 and 8-12 Hz) and beta (12-20 Hz) during the first reach success. Results Combination therapy after ischaemic stroke significantly improved motor and neurological functions compared to monotherapy and vehicle controls. The neural oscillations revealed a significant increase in theta power in the injured motor cortex after combination therapy when compared to that with monotherapy and control groups. The significant increase in the cross-correlation between hemispheres in the combination therapy group over monotherapy indicating an increased synchronised functional connectivity between the injured (left) and uninjured motor (right) cortices. Interestingly, VPA as monotherapy did not significantly reduce infarct volume compared to the vehicle controls. Furthermore, the therapeutic efficacy of monotherapies with VPA and early-onset CIMT (initiated immediately post-stroke) showed limited efficacy in promoting motor and neurological recovery. Conclusion In conclusion, the study demonstrates that VPA combined with physical rehabilitative training (CIMT) enhances functional recovery by enhancing inter-hemispheric functional connectivity and represents a promising therapeutic strategy to alleviate persistent post-stroke motor deficits.

papers.title: Validating the standard model of diffusion MRI in white matter with numerical substrates.
papers.authors: Nguyen-Duc J, Uhl Q, Oliveira R, Rafael-Patiño J, Jelescu IO.
papers.abstract: The non-invasive estimation of intra- and extracellular microstructural parameters using biophysical models has been a major focus in brain microstructure imaging with MRI. The Standard Model (SM) of diffusion in white matter (WM) provides a unifying framework for various modelling approaches, representing axons as impermeable sticks embedded within a locally anisotropic extra-axonal space. However, the SM relies on simplifying assumptions that may not hold in realistic WM tissue, as they do not take into account axonal undulations, beading, the presence of glial cells, or membrane permeability. In this work, we investigate how SM parameter estimates, derived using the Standard Model Imaging (SMI) framework, behave when the model is applied to realistic numerical WM substrates generated by the CATERPillar tool. Specifically, we vary (i) axonal morphological features such as beading and undulations, (ii) axonal packing density, (iii) orientation dispersion, (iv) membrane permeability of axons and astrocytes separately, (v) myelin volume fraction, and (vi) diffusion time. In each part of the analysis, different noise levels are introduced. Our findings enable users to identify potential biases introduced by varying conditions and to adjust their interpretations accordingly.

papers.title: Multicompartmental hemorrhage: A high-risk pattern associated with increased risk for progression in TBI patients.
papers.authors: Tomihiro M, Nguyen PD, Nahmias J, Grigorian A, Habib G, Chung J, Zhang B, Carceroni L, Suzuki MA, Kwon A, Roberts T, Jebbia M, Swentek L.
papers.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
papers.abstract: Background Traumatic brain injury (TBI) with intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) often requires repeat head computed tomography (CT) imaging to monitor for bleed progression. While prior literature has explored patient-level factors, data on the impact of ICH morphologies (subdural [SDH], epidural [EDH], intraparenchymal [IPH], intraventricular [IVH], and multicompartment hemorrhage [MCH]) on radiographic ICH progression remains unclear. We hypothesized that MCH and IVH would have an increased associated risk of progression. Methods This retrospective (2021-2023) single-center cohort included adults (≥18 y) with TBI-related ICH who underwent initial and repeat head CT. Patients were stratified into radiographic progression versus no-progression cohorts, with progression defined as new or enlarging hemorrhage on attending radiologist interpretation of follow-up head CT. The primary outcome was the rate of radiographic progression for each ICH type. MCH was defined as the presence of two or more ICH types. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to evaluate the association between each ICH type and radiographic progression, adjusting for age, mechanism of injury, Injury Severity Score, Glasgow Coma Scale on arrival, trauma-bay intubation, and preinjury antithrombotic exposure. Results Of the 817 patients with ICH on initial head CT and documented repeat CT, 401 (49.1%) had radiographic progression. Patients with progression were younger (58 vs. 62 y, p=0.027), more frequently male (71.3% vs. 63.7%, p=0.020), and had similar antithrombotic exposure (15.2% vs. 14.2%, p=0.678). Craniotomy/craniectomy was more frequent among those with progression (21.2% vs. 8.2%, p<0.001). On multivariable analysis, MCH demonstrated the strongest associated risk for progression (odds ratio [OR] 5.60, 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.36-9.33, p<0.001), whereas IPH (OR 2.02, CI: 0.86-4.75, p=0.108), SDH, EDH, and IVH were not independently associated with radiographic ICH progression. Conclusions MCH was independently associated with radiographic ICH progression. This higher-risk hemorrhage pattern may warrant closer neurological monitoring. Level of evidence Prognostic/Epidemiologic; Level III.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Approach to Outpatient Healthcare of People With Clinically Severe Obesity, According to Pathophysiological and Environmental Aspects: A Critical Review.
papers.authors: Balbino KP, Cândido FG, Coelho OGL, Hermsdorff HHM.
papers.abstract: Severe obesity (SO), defined as a BMI ≥40 kg m-2 or ≥35 kg m-2 with comorbidities, is a complex chronic condition that poses major challenges to clinical management. Current evidence on the pathophysiological and environmental factors influencing outpatient care for people with SO (PSO) is synthesized and analyzed in this review. A literature search covering the past 10 years was conducted, including scientific articles and guidelines from scientific societies addressing these factors. The evidence suggests that conventional outpatient approaches are often insufficient for PSO, because they fail to address the complex biological, behavioral, and environmental mechanisms sustaining SO. Clinically meaningful weight loss often requires reductions of more than 10%, 15%, or even 20%; long-term success rates remain low among individuals treated with nonpharmacological or nonsurgical approaches alone. Genetic predisposition plays a central role, including rare monogenic and syndromic forms associated with early-onset obesity and poorer response to nontargeted therapies, as well as polygenic obesity. Dysfunctions in the leptin-melanocortin pathway also may impair appetite regulation and modify sensory, endocrine, and neural responses related to food intake. People with SO may also present with hedonic hunger and emotional or uncontrolled eating, in addition to higher rates of eating disorders, depression, and anxiety, which contribute to weight regain. The increasing prevalence of SO reinforces the need for a comprehensive, individualized, and multidisciplinary approach that incorporates pathophysiological and environmental determinants into care. Improving outcomes in SO depends not only on expanding therapeutic options but also on better training healthcare teams to recognize the multifactorial mechanisms underlying treatment resistance and weight regain. A structured, person-centered outpatient framework is proposed that integrates biological, psychosocial, and environmental determinants of SO, along with practical clinical tools to support individualized management and improve long-term care.

papers.title: Neuronavigated dual-target transcranial magnetic stimulation for schizophrenia negative symptoms.
papers.authors: Wei Y, Wang J, Tang X, Qian Z, Xu L, Cui H, Song Y, Zhu H, Ju M, Long B, Zhai W, Zeng L, Jiao X, Lan X, Wei X, Tang Y, Wang J, Zhang T.
papers.abstract: Negative symptoms in schizophrenia severely impair function and quality of life, yet respond poorly to current therapies. This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial aimed to investigate the efficacy of neuronavigated dual-target repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) over the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (rDLPFC) and cerebellum for improving negative symptoms in early-stage psychosis (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04853485). Participants with first-episode schizophrenia or clinical high-risk for psychosis were enrolled from Shanghai Mental Health Center and Suzhou Guangji Hospital. Participants were randomly assigned to either a real or sham group under MRI-guided neuronavigation, targeting rDLPFC with 1Hz at 100% motor threshold(MT), cerebellar with intermittent theta burst stimulation(iTBS) at 120% MT for 20 consecutive days. Clinical assessments were conducted at baseline(T0), 10-session(T1), 20-session(T2) and one month after the intervention(T3). Cognition and MRI were evaluated at T0 and T2. The primary outcome was change of negative subscale score of the Positive and Negative Symptoms Scale(PANSS), while secondary outcomes included alterations in other PANSS subscale scores and fronto-cerebellar circuit functional connectivity. In total, 75 participants were included in the intention-to-treat analysis (36 active, 39 sham). The pre-specified primary linear mixed-effects analysis revealed a non-significant group-by-time interaction for PANSS negative subscale scores (F(3,174.6)=1.45, p=0.230). At the 4-week endpoint (T2), the nominal unadjusted between-group p-value was 0.049; after Sidak correction for multiple comparisons, the adjusted mean difference was -2.48 points (95% CI -4.99 to 0.03, adjusted p=0.150, Cohen's d=-0.51). Descriptive uncorrected t-tests indicated greater negative-symptom reductions in the active group at T1 and T2, and the 4-week negative-symptom response rate (≥50% reduction) was higher under real rTMS (χ2=9.5, p=0.002). A significant group-by-time interaction was observed for PANSS positive subscale scores (F(3,172.0)=3.26, p=0.023). Both groups exhibited substantial within-group symptom improvement. Resting-state fMRI demonstrated group-by-time interactions within cerebello-temporal, parahippocampal, caudate, and parietal networks (FWE-corrected p<0.05), and negative-symptom change correlated with cerebello-caudate connectivity (r=0.33, p=0.026). These findings suggest neuronavigated dual-target rTMS over rDLPFC and cerebellum may be associated with numerical improvements in negative symptoms in early-stage psychosis.

papers.title: Phase-locked closed-loop ultrasound stimulation of hippocampal slow gamma modulates CA3-CA1 coherence and improves spatial memory in APP/PS1 mice.
papers.authors: Xie Z, Ji H, Karadas M, Zhang Y, Yuan Y.
papers.abstract: Objective. Impaired hippocampal slow gamma oscillations and CA3-CA1 dysfunction may contribute to spatial memory deficits in early Alzheimer's disease (AD). This study examined whether phase-locked closed-loop transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS) could modulate CA3-CA1 activity and improve memory.Approach. A closed-loop TUS system was developed that uses the phase of endogenous slow gamma (30-45 Hz) rhythms in CA3 local field potentials as a trigger. Acute experiments were performed to assess phase-dependent neural responses. Normal rats received 14 d of stimulation to examine circuit connectivity and behavior. APP/PS1 mice received 14 d of peak-phase stimulation to test behavioral and electrophysiological effects.Main results. Acute experiments showed that both stimulation phase and stimulation number jointly modulated neural responses. Peak-phase and random-phase stimulation increased slow gamma power and cross-frequency coupling, while peak-phase stimulation also decreased sample entropy and increased CA3-CA1 coherence. In normal rats, behavioral performance did not differ among groups after 14 d, but task-related CA3-CA1 slow gamma coherence was higher in the peak-phase group. In APP/PS1 mice, peak-phase stimulation improved Y-maze spontaneous alternation and novel object location discrimination, alongside increased CA1 power, CA3-CA1 coherence, cross-frequency coupling, and spike-field coherence, all of which were positively correlated with behavioral scores.Significance. These findings indicate that phase-locked closed-loop ultrasound stimulation modulates hippocampal slow gamma activity and CA3-CA1 connectivity in a phase-dependent manner and improves spatial memory in an AD mouse model, supporting oscillation-guided noninvasive neuromodulation as a potential intervention strategy.

papers.title: Early disruptions in brain capillary blood flow control in a mouse model of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.authors: Hariharan A, Vigderman A, Isaacs DP, Weir N, Park G, Edwards S, Longden TA.
papers.abstract: In Alzheimer's disease (AD), vascular dysfunction and impaired control of brain blood flow can disrupt cellular bioenergetics decades before cognitive decline. Identifying the earliest vascular changes is therefore critical for developing therapies that intervene before the cascading events leading to neuronal decline. Brain energy supply is dynamically controlled by the cerebral vasculature, where capillary thin-strand pericytes are emerging as key players. We recently identified a central role for ATP-sensitive potassium (K+, KATP) channels in enabling thin-strand pericytes to sense local neuronal activity and generate hyperpolarizing signals that are transmitted via capillary endothelial cells to upstream arterioles, eliciting increases in blood flow. Importantly, thin-strand pericyte KATP channels are the centerpiece of an electro-metabolic "energy switch" mechanism that couples decreases in local glucose to hyperemia, providing a failsafe to ensure continual energy substrate supply to support neuronal function. Disruption of this mechanism could therefore precipitate an imbalance between demand and supply, creating an energy gap for neurons that leads to deleterious consequences. We demonstrate that capillary control of blood flow is disrupted in the early stages of disease progression in mice expressing familial AD mutations (5xFAD). Transgenic 5xFAD mice exhibit early disruption of capillary signaling, beginning with dysfunctional endothelial inward rectifier K+ (Kir)2.1 channels at 2-4 mo, disabling transmission of KATP-mediated signals to upstream blood flow control machinery, followed by direct impairment of pericyte KATP channel function by 6-8 mo. Together, these deficits cause early and sustained failure of electrical signaling from deep capillary pericytes to upstream arterioles and arteriole-capillary transition (ACT) zone vessels, limiting KATP-dependent energy-switch-mediated blood flow control. Our findings define a temporal and mechanistic framework linking familial AD mutations to early capillary signaling dysfunction and highlight preservation of capillary blood flow control as a potential therapeutic target to protect against downstream effects of amyloid β accumulation.

papers.title: Bone microarchitecture, density, and strength assessment in automotive trauma patients using HR-pQCT: a pilot study.
papers.authors: Guerrero Sanchez GB, Cattell KL, Hsu FC, Madrid Fuentes DA, Armstrong WM, Devane KS, Popuri K, Beg MF, May AK, Torres Fajardo RA, Lopez R, Kiani B, Martin RS, Miller AN, Taylor AB, Davidson BA, Sink JI, Stitzel JD, Weaver AA.
papers.abstract: Objective Automotive trauma patients enrolled in the Crash Injury Research and Engineering Network (CIREN) typically undergo computed tomography (CT) imaging as part of emergency care. HR-pQCT is a noninvasive imaging technique that enables assessment of bone microarchitecture at the peripheral sites. CT and HR-pQCT can be used to estimate volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) and strength via finite element analysis (FEA). However, HR-pQCT's superior resolution (approximately 10 times higher than conventional clinical CT scanners) captures in vivo trabecular and cortical microarchitecture, enabling high fidelity FEA. This study examines HR-pQCT-derived bone microarchitecture and strength measurements in relation to fracture patterns, bone-related comorbidities, and CT-derived vBMD in CIREN trauma patients, while providing foundational evidence to support HR-pQCT use following motor vehicle crashes (MVC) and pedestrian crashes. Methods Nine automotive trauma patients (ages 17-76; 78% female) enrolled at Atrium Health Wake Forest Baptist Medical Center from the National Highway Safety Administration's CIREN study participated in the HR-pQCT pilot study. HR-pQCT scans were acquired within 1-12 months following the patient's MVC (n = 7) or pedestrian crash (n = 2). Scans were acquired at four sites: 1) distal tibia, 2) diaphyseal tibia, 3) distal radius, and 4) diaphyseal radius. HR-pQCT normative percentiles were determined using Indiana University's calculator. Descriptive statistics were used to present HR-pQCT musculoskeletal outcomes based on bone-related comorbidities, BMI, and fracture incidence. Pearson correlations were performed between HR-pQCT-derived distal tibia and radius total vBMD and CT-derived total vBMD at the spine and femoral compartments. Results At the distal tibia, participants without tibia and fibula fractures tended to show greater mean cortical thickness (1.63 ± 0.38 versus 1.15 ± 0.05 mm), cortical area (146.24 ± 46.07 versus 103.70 ± 1.70 mm2 ), cortical vBMD (943.83 ± 79.18 versus 861.05 ± 26.52 mg HA/cm3 ), and bone strength (10.25 ± 3.72 versus 7.00 ± 0.70 kN). Additionally, HR-pQCT-derived distal tibia total vBMD demonstrated a strong positive correlation with CT-derived femoral head total vBMD (r = 0.766; p = 0.045). Normative percentiles showed that participants with bone-related comorbidities had lower bone microarchitectural and strength percentiles than the group without comorbidities. Conclusion This study demonstrates the viability of HR-pQCT for characterizing bone microarchitecture, strength, and density in automotive trauma patients and identifying differences that might relate to fracture and bone-related comorbidities. These preliminary findings support incorporating HR-pQCT imaging into automotive crash research due to its ability to provide detailed cortical and trabecular microarchitectural measurements that are not available from clinical CT.

papers.title: Environmental neurotoxicants as accelerators of brain ageing: exposomic mechanisms linking pollution to amyloidogenesis and Alzheimer's disease.
papers.authors: Patel S, Paliwal A, Jha SK, Singh R, Mishra AK.
papers.journal: International journal of environmental health research
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder characterised by progressive cognitive decline, amyloid-β (Aβ) deposition, tau hyperphosphorylation, synaptic dysfunction, and chronic neuroinflammation. While rare familial cases are genetically driven, most AD is sporadic, underscoring the critical role of environmental determinants. Emerging evidence from epidemiological, experimental, and exposomic studies identifies environmental neurotoxicants, including air pollutants, heavy metals, pesticides, and emerging contaminants such as micro- and nanoplastics, as significant accelerators of brain ageing and AD pathogenesis.These toxicants access the central nervous system via systemic circulation, olfactory translocation, and gut-brain axis interactions, converging on shared pathogenic mechanisms such as oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired proteostasis, and neuroimmune activation. Together, these processes promote amyloidogenic processing of amyloid precursor protein, enhance Aβ aggregation, and drive tau pathology, accelerating neurodegenerative cascades. Notably, early-life exposures induce persistent epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming, increasing lifelong vulnerability, particularly in genetically susceptible markers such as APOE ε4 carriers. Although preclinical models robustly demonstrate pollutant-induced AD-like phenotypes, translation into clinical interventions remains limited. Integrating environmental exposures into AD pathogenesis frameworks highlights the exposome as a modifiable risk factor and emphasizes the urgent need for longitudinal human studies, mechanistic validation, and preventive public health strategies targeting environmental risk reduction.

papers.title: Two clusters of brain regions with distinct age-related profiles of functional connectivity in autism spectrum disorder.
papers.authors: Li X, Zuo F, Cheng Y, Perkins K, Cao F.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: Brain functional connectivity changes throughout development, and individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may follow trajectories that differ from those of typically developing controls. Using large multisite resting-state fMRI cross-sectional datasets, we examined how functional connectivity differences between ASD and typically developing controls change across a broad age range of 5 to 64 y. A data-driven analysis identified two spatially distributed clusters of cortical regions showing distinct age-related profiles of ASD-TD connectivity differences. Cluster 1 was marked by consistent hypoconnectivity across ages, suggesting a stable neural signature of ASD. Cluster 2 was characterized by hypoconnectivity in childhood that gradually diminished with age, suggesting a temporary delay profile. These clusters were systematically organized along the sensory-association axis. Cluster 1 mainly involved lower-rank sensory and sensorimotor cortices, while Cluster 2 mainly involved higher-rank association cortices. Brain-behavior analyses revealed greater and broader ASD symptom associations across ages in the consistent hypoconnectivity profile than the delay profile. Further subtype analyses suggested that social-affect symptoms were associated with greater hypoconnectivity than repetitive behavior symptoms in both clusters. Spatial correlation analyses with neurotransmitter maps revealed associations of Cluster 1 with mGluR5 and of Cluster 2 with GABAA α5, providing insight into the neurobiological basis of the two clusters. In a cross-disorder validation analysis, applying the same analytic framework to attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder did not reveal comparable results. Together, these findings suggest that ASD-related functional connectivity alterations are developmentally heterogeneous and organized along the cortical hierarchy, providing a developmental perspective for understanding the neurobiology of ASD.

papers.title: Mechanistic versus descriptive interpretation of brain activity pattern reconstruction.
papers.authors: Jung K, Eickhoff SB, Patil KR.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: The geometric eigenmodes, derived from the shape of the cortical surface, have been suggested as a better model for explaining brain function due to their high accuracy in reconstructing patterns of both spontaneous and stimulus-evoked brain activity patterns captured by functional MRI, when contrasted with alternative models including structural connectome derived bases. While a descriptive representation offers valuable utility for neuroimaging studies, it is necessary to examine the extent to which it supports a mechanistic explanation for human brain function. Although the observation that geometric eigenmodes accurately fit brain activity is intriguing, we argue that accepting them as a model of brain function risks conflating descriptive and mechanistic interpretations. While a representation that effectively describes the underlying geometry is inherently adept at fitting patterns within that geometric space; it does not necessarily shed light on mechanisms that give rise to the brain's functional attributes. To this end, we provide two lines of empirical results: a) geometric eigenmodes demonstrate a high flexibility when fit to a range of manipulated patterns, and b) localized parcel-based representations can reconstruct activity patterns as well. Based on those results, theoretical considerations, and previous data, we argue that more consideration is needed regarding the complementary roles of descriptive representation and mechanistic explanation in neuroimaging research. While we recognize the potential role of the brain's geometry in influencing its dynamics, assertions regarding its efficacy should be weighed against its inherent lack of specificity, biological interpretability, and anatomical evidence.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal AI-based modeling of gene regulation and variant effects in the developing human brain using Seal.
papers.authors: Hao Y, Park CY, Theesfeld CL, Troyanskaya OG.
papers.abstract: Understanding how genetic variation shapes gene regulation in the developing human brain remains a central challenge in neuroscience, particularly in transient cell types and developmental stages where data are limited. We present Seal, an interpretable artificial intelligence (AI) transfer learning framework for genome-based modeling of gene expression and variant effects with spatiotemporal resolution across 26 regions, 30 cell types and 7 developmental stages. Seal predictions provide mechanistic interpretation by linking variants to transcriptional regulators in a spatiotemporal context. Applying Seal to genome-wide association studies, we identify shared and distinct regulatory architectures across six neuropsychiatric conditions that align with clinical trajectories. In the Simons Simplex Collection autism cohort whole-genome data, Seal uncovers a significant burden of de novo regulatory variants in transient fetal excitatory neurons, revealing cell-type-specific and stage-specific effects. By connecting genetic variation to spatiotemporal regulatory programs, Seal offers a general framework for uncovering mechanisms of human brain development and disease.

papers.title: An aging-sensitive secreted phospholipase confers neuroprotection and cognitive resilience.
papers.authors: Vicidomini C, Goode TD, Yu R, Mehta I, McAvoy KM, Beveridge CH, Randolph CE, Iyer SN, Victor MB, Leary N, Evans L, Steinbaugh MJ, Lai ZW, Lyon MC, San Silvestre MRF, Tosoni G, Ayyildiz D, Ho Sui S, Yamamoto K, Murakami M, Salta E, Tsai LH, Chopra G, Sahay A.
papers.abstract: Cognitive reserve theory posits that compensatory mechanisms during aging stave off cognitive decline and lower risk for Alzheimer's disease. Here, in a screen for hippocampal dentate granule cell (DGC) synapse loss-induced factors in mice, we identified a secreted phospholipase, Pla2g2f, whose expression increases in DGCs during aging and is associated with cognitive resilience in humans. Pla2g2f deletion in DGCs exacerbates aging-associated pathophysiological changes, including synapse loss, inflammatory microglia, reactive astrogliosis, impaired neurogenesis, lipid dysregulation, lipid droplet accumulation and hippocampal-dependent memory loss. Conversely, boosting Pla2g2f in DGCs during aging is sufficient to prevent these pathophysiological alterations in hippocampal-cortical circuits, protect memory and prophylactically modify trajectory of cognitive decline. Mutagenesis of the catalytic site of PLA2G2F prevented lipid droplet mobilization and reduction of reactive gliosis and inflammatory microglia. Neuronal PLA2G2F mediates intercellular signaling to decrease lipid droplet and cholesterol ester load in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived microglia. Our findings implicate PLA2G2F as a compensatory neuroprotective broadcast signal that maintains lipid homeostasis to counteract aging-associated cognitive decline.

papers.title: Periventricular gradient pathology is linked to ependymal reactivity and cell adhesion disruption in multiple sclerosis.
papers.authors: Groh AMR, Afanasiev E, Thevakumaran R, Creeggan F, Callahan-Martin L, Bigotte M, Yaqubi M, Gertsvolf J, Pei J, Wu H, de Vos J, Aalders MCG, Zandee S, Prat A, Rudko DA, Stratton JA.
papers.abstract: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-adjacent brain areas are especially vulnerable to diffuse degeneration in multiple sclerosis (MS). Surface-in gradients arising from CSF-borne cytotoxic factors have been proposed to predict disease relapses independent of white matter lesions. Yet, whether such factors disrupt ependymal cells to penetrate the ventricular border in MS remains unknown. Here, using ultra-high-field magnetic resonance imaging-guided histology, electron microscopy and single-nucleus multiomics, we found that ependymal pathology correlates with periventricular gradients and involves an immune-reactive state marked by transporter and junctional protein dysregulation. We further defined the gene regulatory networks underpinning the MS ependymal state and predicted ligands known to be enriched in MS CSF that could drive the emergence of this state. One of the candidates, IFNγ, increased murine ependymal permeability in vivo, indicating that CSF ligands can modulate ependymal function and regional inflammation. These findings identify CSF-driven ependymal dysfunction as a contributor to periventricular pathology in MS.

papers.title: A half-center oscillator regulates sleep pressure.
papers.authors: Hasenhuetl PS, Sarnataro R, Vrontou E, Rorsman HO, Talbot CB, Brain R, Miesenböck G.
papers.abstract: Changes in oscillatory neural dynamics reflect-but may not necessarily determine-transitions between sleep stages and variations in sleep pressure. Here we show that sleep-control neurons innervating the dorsal fan-shaped body of Drosophila (dFBNs) produce slow-wave activity (SWA) that is causally linked to sleep. The dFBN ensemble contains bistable cells whose membrane voltages oscillate between hyperpolarized DOWN and depolarized UP states. The oscillations rely on interhemispheric competition of two half-centers connected by inhibitory glutamatergic synapses. dFBN-restricted interference with glutamate release disrupts SWA and baseline as well as rebound sleep, whereas the optogenetic replay of SWA induces sleep. dFBNs generate SWA throughout the sleep-wake cycle (despite mutual antagonism with arousing dopaminergic neurons) and adjust its power to sleep need via sleep history-dependent increases in excitability and homeostatic synaptic depression. The oscillatory format permits a continuous encoding of sleep pressure but requires mechanisms that convert the amplitude-modulated signal into binary sleep-wake states.

papers.title: Polygenic scores for longevity in relation to brain MRI measures in a cohort of 70-year-olds.
papers.authors: Seidu NM, Lindberg O, Kern S, Rydén L, Wahlund LO, Waern M, Mohanty R, Cedres N, Zetterberg H, Blennow K, Erhag HF, Zettergren A, Westman E, Holstege H, Skoog I.
papers.abstract: Population-based studies on the relation between polygenic longevity scores (PGLSs) and specific brain regions on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are few. We aimed to investigate this relationship in a population of 70-year-olds from Gothenburg, Sweden (N = 675). We constructed two PGLSs (one with and one without the APOE locus) using longevity GWAS summary statistics. MRI outcomes included total grey matter, white matter (WM), WM hyperintensities (WMHs), subcortical volumes, small vessel disease (SVD) score, cortical thicknesses, and fractional anisotropy (FA) fibre tracts. We adjusted for sex, age, principal components, and sex interactions, and corrected for multiple comparisons. We found no associations in the total sample. In males, both PGLSs were associated with smaller WMHs volume and lower SVD burden, and a thicker cortex of pars triangularis, pars opercularis, and insula. Our findings suggest a possible link between genetic propensity for longevity and lower cerebrovascular burden and certain cortical grey matter areas in males.

papers.title: Retrieval-induced forgetting and facilitation across the Alzheimer's disease continuum: Behavioral and neuroanatomical evidence from a recognition-based paradigm.
papers.authors: Di Domenico C, Bonarota S, Caruso G, Sperati S, Di Lorenzo F, Rodini M, Caltagirone C, Koch G, Giove F, Bozzali M, Serra L.
papers.abstract: Objective The aim of the present study was to investigate facilitation (FAC) and retrieval-induced forgetting (RIF) during episodic memory retrieval across the Alzheimer's disease (AD) continuum and to examine their gray matter correlates in verbal and visual recognition tasks. Method One hundred participants (28 AD, 29 amnestic mild cognitive impairment, 23 subjective cognitive decline [SCD], 20 healthy subjects) completed a modified retrieval-practice paradigm (mRPP) involving verbal and visual recognition tasks, a comprehensive neuropsychological battery, and 3T magnetic resonance imaging. FAC and RIF were computed at the group level and via individual proxy scores, and voxel-based morphometry was used to assess the association between mRPP indices and regional gray matter volumes. Results The verbal mRPP showed reduced overall recognition in AD compared with healthy subjects (p = .003 - ηp ² = 0.23). A robust FAC effect in AD, amnestic mild cognitive impairment, and SCD was observed, whereas RIF emerged only in SCD, suggesting intact inhibitory control at the earliest stage and its disruption with disease progression (p < .001 - ηp ² = 0.48). The visual mRPP showed a strong FAC effect across all groups, with no RIF, indicating modality-specific reliance on recognition-based retrieval (p < .001 - ηp ² = 0.63). Voxel-based morphometry analyses revealed distinct gray matter correlates across groups and tasks: Verbal RIF was negatively associated with frontotemporal regions in AD patients and parieto-occipital regions in healthy subjects, while visual indices showed widespread associations with temporal, subcortical, cerebellar, and sensorimotor regions, particularly in amnestic mild cognitive impairment and SCD groups. Conclusions This study shows shared and modality-specific brain mechanisms of retrieval practice across AD stages. Preserved compensatory processes in SCD individuals give way to progressive regional disruption, supporting early, modality-tailored, and multimodal cognitive interventions to enhance cognition and delay cognitive decline. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

papers.title: Safety and efficacy of high-current tTIS targeting left sgACC for major depressive disorder: A randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial.
papers.authors: Wang M, Wu W, Zheng Q, Zhou H, Ren J, Gou H, Meng X, Cui G, Sun J, Zhou J, Chen X, Guo J, Li S, He Z, Ge D, Wang G, Yuan Q, Jiao D, Yu X, Wang B, Zhang M, Chang C, Zeng GQ, Zhang X.
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a leading cause of disability, and non-invasive stimulation of deep brain circuits such as the subgenual anterior cingulate cortex (sgACC) remains challenging. This randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial recruits 96 adults with moderate-to-severe MDD who received 10 sessions of 2 mA low-current, 15 mA high-current, or sham transcranial temporal interference stimulation (tTIS) targeting the left sgACC. The high-current group shows significantly greater reductions in depressive symptoms (17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale [HDRS-17] score) post-treatment and at 1-month follow-up compared with sham and outperforms the low-current group post-treatment. Exploratory Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) analyses suggest improved sleep quality in both active groups, whereas anxiety outcomes show no intergroup differences. High-current tTIS is safe and well tolerated, with only transient tingling. These findings provide preliminary evidence that sgACC-targeted tTIS relieves depressive symptoms safely, with more robust short-to medium-term effects observed under the 15 mA protocol. This trial registers on Chictr.org.cn (ChiCTR2400094971).

papers.title: Genome-wide CRISPR screen reveals that Wnt signaling regulates lipid accumulation in APOE4 oligodendrocytes.
papers.authors: Akay LA, Bright A, Dong D, Smith ED, Hurt RC, Boix CA, Louderback K, Medrano J, Sun D, Lin H, King O, Welch GM, Nawaid H, Agbas E, Jiang A, Bubnys A, Cheng JX, Blanchard JW, Tsai LH.
papers.abstract: APOE4 is the strongest genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer's disease, yet the cellular mechanisms linking APOE variants to disease risk remain unclear. We previously found that APOE4 expression causes lipid droplet accumulation in oligodendrocytes, reducing myelination, but the underlying mechanisms were unknown. Using a genome-wide CRISPR screen and assay for transposase-accessible chromatin (ATAC) sequencing in human-induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived oligodendrocytes, we identified decreased Wnt signaling and overactive glycogen synthase kinase-3 beta (GSK3B) as key regulators of lipid-droplet accumulation. Genetic and pharmacological inhibition of GSK3B reduced lipid droplets in APOE4 oligodendrocytes and increased myelination in three-dimensional iPSC-derived brain organoids. Pharmacological GSK3B inhibition also reduced lipid droplets and improved myelination in APOE4;PS19 tau transgenic mice. Together, these findings establish a mechanistic framework linking Wnt/GSK3B signaling to APOE4-driven disruptions in oligodendrocyte lipid metabolism and myelination, pointing to GSK3B as a potential therapeutic target for APOE4-associated Alzheimer's disease.

papers.title: Predicting individual differences in social functioning from functional connectomes in children with autism spectrum disorder.
papers.authors: Li A, Zhang J, Yu C, Tan L, Yi A, Xiao Y.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by profound heterogeneity in social functioning. While previous studies using group-level comparisons and predefined regions of interest have identified neural correlates of social deficits in ASD, the neural basis of individual differences in social functioning remains unclear. Here, we applied connectome-based predictive modeling to resting-state functional MRI data from 65 children with ASD aged 1.5-8 years (mean age = 4.23 years) to predict individual differences in social functioning assessed by the personal-social subscale of the Griffiths Development Scales (GDS). Results showed that whole-brain functional connectivity significantly predicted personal-social scores. The positive predictive network was dominated by connections within the default mode network, with the left precuneus emerging as a core hub. In contrast, the negative predictive network mainly involved inter-network connections, particularly between the frontoparietal and sensorimotor networks. In an independent cohort of 27 children with ASD aged 1.25-8 years (mean age = 3.31 years), the positive-edge model showed a significant association with personal-social scores, whereas the negative-edge and combined models did not. These findings suggest that intrinsic large-scale brain network organization is associated with individual differences in social functioning in children with ASD, highlighting the potential of network-level approaches for characterizing neurodevelopmental heterogeneity and supporting future precision-oriented research.

papers.title: A comparative study of modified suanzaoren decoction versus estazolam in chronic insomnia disorder: Clinical outcomes and thalamocortical network changes.
papers.authors: Wang R, Han Y, Chen L, Lv D, Yao P, Guo Z, Guo W.
papers.abstract: Chronic insomnia disorder (CID) is associated with widespread abnormalities in thalamic functional connectivity (FC). For CID patients with the yin-deficiency and fire-excess syndrome, Modified Suanzaoren Decoction (MSZRD) and estazolam are common treatments, but their longitudinal associations with thalamic networks remain unclear. This study was a non-randomized, patient-preference controlled trial. Eighty-two CID patients with yin-deficiency and fire-excess syndrome received a 6-week treatment with either MSZRD or estazolam based on preference. Additionally, 54 healthy controls (HCs) were recruited for baseline comparison. Clinical scales, polysomnography, and resting-state fMRI data were collected pre- and post-treatment. Using the Human Brainnetome Atlas, the thalamus was parcellated into eight subregions. We examined baseline group differences and longitudinal FC changes, and identified genes associated with the baseline FC alterations for enrichment analysis. At baseline, CID patients showed significantly increased FC in pathways involving the medial pre-frontal thalamus, posterior parietal thalamus, lateral pre-frontal thalamus, and caudal temporal thalamus with multiple cortical regions. After treatment, the MSZRD group showed greater improvement than the estazolam group on subjective and objective measures. While FC decreased in the MSZRD group between the left occipital thalamus and right middle frontal gyrus, and between the right occipital thalamus and right angular gyrus, it increased in the estazolam group for these connections. Enrichment analysis of genes associated with baseline FC alterations identified pathways related to synaptic organization, cytoskeletal stability, and metabolism. These findings provide preliminary evidence that CID is associated with enhanced thalamocortical connectivity consistent with the thalamus-centric hyperarousal model, and that MSZRD and estazolam show different clinical and neural correlates. However, due to the non-randomized design and baseline FC differences, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in future randomized mechanistic studies.

papers.title: A comprehensive review of the neurobehavioral and neurotoxic effects of 6PPD-Q in fish, rodents, and humans.
papers.authors: Ivantsova E, Lu A, Martyniuk CJ.
papers.abstract: N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N'-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine (6PPD) is a widely used tire additive that undergoes environmental transformation to 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q), which is ubiquitously detected in environmental matrices. Increasing evidence demonstrates that exposure to 6PPD-Q adversely affects organisms through neurobehavioral disruption and neurotoxicity. While studies document behavioral abnormalities and molecular alterations, a comprehensive synthesis linking these outcomes remains limited. The objective of this review was to synthesize current literature reporting neurobehavioral and neurotoxic effects of 6PPD-Q in fish, rodents, and humans using experimental and computational approaches. Using PRISMA guidelines, a search was conducted in PubMed and Google Scholar using several key phrases related to 6PPD-Q and neurotoxicity, capturing 1874 records. Relevant articles were assessed by full-text review for criteria eligibility, and the final review included 27 articles. In fish, exposure to 6PPD-Q can alter neurobehaviors like locomotor activity, anxiety-like responses, social and aggressive behaviors, and disturbances in circadian-regulated activities. Such behavioral outcomes correspond closely with neurotransmitter imbalance, neuroendocrine disruption, blood-brain barrier dysfunction, and transcriptome changes affecting neural signaling pathways. In rodents, repeated or chronic exposure to 6PPD-Q leads to neuronal damage, cognitive impairment, anxiety-like behavior, and memory deficits. Human biomonitoring and mechanistic studies further associate 6PPD-Q exposure with oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and molecular responses relevant to neurological diseases. Leveraging the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database, computational analysis revealed entities associated with 6PPD-Q in the database were related to Alzheimer's disease, dopaminergic synapses, neurotrophin signaling pathways, and Parkinson's disease. Taken together, data suggests that 6PPD-Q may interfere with neuronal signaling, connectivity, and plasticity, leading to behavioral deficits. Based on predictive docking scores using fish, rodent, and human orthologs, 6PPD-Q may interact with tyrosine hydroxylase and L-dopa decarboxylase which can potentially lead to disrupted dopamine biosynthesis pathways. Given the widespread environmental presence of 6PPD-Q and its continuous introduction into aquatic ecosystems, characterizing such mechanisms is critical for improving ecological and human health risk assessments.

papers.title: Peripheral pathway rerouting shapes whole-brain functional network.
papers.authors: Hu JJ, Xiang YT, Huo BB, Zuo YF, Peng CY, He-Wang, Wu JJ, Zheng MX, Xu JG.
papers.abstract: Pathway rerouting is critical for severe peripheral nerve injury (PNI), which induces widespread neuroplastic alterations within the central nervous system, yet whether different rerouting approaches differentially affect whole-brain functional networks remains unknown. The present study investigated alterations in brain network organization following different peripheral pathway rerouting after PNI. Adult Sprague-Dawley rats underwent complete left brachial plexus transection and were assigned to nerve repair, end-to-end nerve transfer, end-to-side nerve transfer, or untreated PNI groups. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging was acquired 7 months after surgery. Whole-brain functional connectivity matrices were constructed, and graph theoretical analysis was performed to assess global and nodal network properties, including global efficiency, nodal efficiency, and small-world characteristics. Rich-club, feeder, and local connections were further analyzed to characterize patterns of network reorganization. The results revealed significant differences in global efficiency, nodal efficiency, small-world organization and feeder connection among the four groups. Compared with the other reconstruction procedures, end-to-end nerve transfer showed reduced global efficiency, impaired small-world organization, lower nodal efficiency in subcortical regions, and increased functional connectivity and feeder connections, indicating reduced efficiency of large-scale information processing. In contrast, end-to-side nerve transfer preserved global efficiency, nodal efficiency, and small-world properties to a greater extent and was accompanied by more extensive increases in functional connectivity. These findings suggest that end-to-end nerve transfer appears to have a negative effect on the order of the whole-brain network, whereas end-to-side nerve transfer better preserves and restores network stability.
